author: Hacker News

title: HEYDUDE Instagram Ad with UF Frat Sparks Backlash Over Sexual Cyberharassment Allegations
content:
A collaborative Instagram post featuring footwear brand HEYDUDE and a University of Florida fraternity has drawn criticism. The post is sparking backlash because of sexual cyberharassment allegations against two former fraternity members.

The controversy centers on the fraternity’s involvement in the campaign, with the allegations prompting a negative response from the public. No further details are provided.
summary: A collaborative Instagram post between footwear line HEYDUDE and a University of Florida frat has sparked backlash. The backlash is due to sexual cyberharassment allegations against two former members of the frat.
author: Wired

title: ICE stored protester photos in Palantir database after tracking them in Maine
content:
DHS agents tracked and intimidated individuals observing ICE activity in Maine and stored information about them in a Palantir‑built database, according to newly unsealed court filings.  

The filings say ICE dumped protester photos into the Palantir database as part of that data collection.
summary: DHS agents tracked and intimidated people observing ICE activity in Maine. The agents stored information about those individuals in a Palantir-built database, according to newly unsealed court filings.
author: Wired

title: Beehiiv raises prices, renaming Scale to Lite and increasing monthly costs
content:
Beehiiv, the creator platform that has gained traction as an alternative to Substack, announced a price increase that has sparked backlash among its users. In a post explaining the change, co‑founder and CEO Tyler Denk said the hike would allow the company to “continue investing in our core platform experience.”

The company is renaming its mid‑range Scale plan to Lite and raising its price by at least $10 per month, depending on subscriber count. For example, creators with up to 10,000 subscribers will now pay $139 per month instead of $109. The Pro plan, formerly called Max, will cost $239 per month.

The price adjustments reflect Beehiiv’s strategy to strengthen its platform, though many users have expressed dissatisfaction with the new rates.
summary: Beehiiv is increasing prices for its creator platform, with the renamed Lite plan rising by at least $10 per month based on subscriber count. CEO Tyler Denk stated the increase will allow the company to continue investing in its core platform experience.
author: The Verge

title: Rivian Q3 deliveries jump 45% as R2 vehicle strategy begins to pay off
content:
Rivian reported its third-quarter production and delivery figures, showing 19,751 vehicles produced and 19,248 delivered. These results mark an 85 percent year-over-year increase in production and a 45 percent jump in deliveries, which the company cites as evidence that its strategy for the more affordable R2 vehicle is beginning to pay off.

The automaker also reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance, projecting deliveries of between 65,000 and 70,000 vehicles. As a direct-to-consumer brand, Rivian uses delivery numbers as a proxy for sales, highlighting the surge as a notable positive development within a challenging industry landscape.
summary: Rivian reported third-quarter production of 19,751 vehicles and deliveries of 19,248, representing an 85 percent year-over-year increase in production. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance to deliver between 65,000 and 70,000 vehicles.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI launches Dots, an enterprise agent platform with avatars
content:
OpenAI has announced Dots, a new enterprise agent platform designed to function as workplace software while also handling personal tasks such as ordering dinner. The platform features anthropomorphic, blobby avatars with customizable names, similar to Meta’s Muse. Currently, users are limited to a single Dots agent, although OpenAI states that multiple agents will be available in the future.

The interface allows users to chat with the agent in one window while following its work in another. The Verge describes the experience as feeling like using workplace software that happens to be capable of casual tasks, emphasizing its primary focus on professional use.
summary: OpenAI announced Dots, a new agent platform featuring customizable anthropomorphic avatars. The software is designed for enterprise use, allowing users to chat with an agent while it performs tasks.
author: The Verge

title: Sling TV drops its one-day cable passes
content:
Dish-owned Sling TV is discontinuing its Sling Pass feature, which previously allowed customers to purchase single-day, weekend, or week-long cable TV programming access. The service enabled users to watch channels such as ESPN and CNN without committing to a full-month subscription.

The Sling Pass option was announced last year but faced immediate legal challenges from Disney and Warner Bros. Discovery. Although a federal judge denied Disney’s request for a preliminary injunction that would have blocked the feature, Sling TV has decided to stop offering it. The company stated that Sling was built to give customers ultimate control over their entertainment.
summary: Dish-owned Sling TV will no longer be offering its Sling Pass feature that allowed people to buy a single day of cable TV programming at a time, as reported by The Desk. The feature was announced last year and offered a day pass, a weekend pass, and a week-long pass option to be able to watch channels like ESPN and CNN without a full-month cable subscription.
author: The Verge

title: Apple to limit Mac full disk access amid AI agent risks
content:
Apple is implementing new restrictions on "full disk access" for Mac users to mitigate the risks associated with AI agents. The company announced on Friday that it is introducing controls designed to ensure that granting an application this level of access requires "very explicit user action."

This update follows a report by TechCrunch and a finding by Inc’s Jason Aten, who discovered that Meta’s Muse AI had access to the contents of his messages despite him not explicitly granting permission on his iPhone or Mac. Meta spokesperson Andy Stone disputed the report, stating that access to Messages is "entirely opt-in."
summary: Apple will add new limits for full disk access on Mac to mitigate risks from AI agents. The change follows a report that Meta's Muse AI accessed the contents of Jason Aten's messages without explicit permission, a claim Meta's spokesperson Andy Stone says is entirely opt-in.
author: The Verge

title: Netflix Ends Director Deals in Strategic Shift Away From Prestige Content
content:
Netflix is ending multiyear production deals with prominent directors such as David Fincher and Shawn Levy, a move that signals a strategic pivot away from prestige content. These partnerships had previously produced many of the streamer’s most critically acclaimed hits. The decision comes as Netflix seeks to maintain its competitive position in the streaming market, particularly with rival studios Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery on the verge of a megamerger that is expected to reshape the entertainment landscape.

As the company charts its path forward, its plan to court subscribers appears to be shifting focus away from high-profile director collaborations.
summary: Netflix has recently ended multiyear production deals with directors such as David Fincher and Shawn Levy. This move indicates a broader strategic pivot as the company prepares for a streaming landscape reshaped by the impending Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery merger.
author: The Verge

title: Meta open sources code to let users build custom Muse AI gadgets
content:
Meta has open-sourced code that allows users to create custom "Muse gadgets" powered by the company's new AI agent. These open-source devices are designed for individuals to build themselves using accessible hardware components.

The company suggests several project ideas, including loading Muse onto a color E Ink display for reminders, attaching it to an HDMI stick for big-screen display, or integrating it into a small touchscreen device to resemble a DIY Muse Charm. Meta explains that builders can program an off-the-shelf ESP32 board or set up a Raspberry Pi using the provided SDKs to connect Muse to various displays, buttons, sensors, and actuators.
summary: Meta has open-sourced code that allows users to create their own Muse gadgets featuring the company's new AI agent. The company suggests projects such as loading Muse on E Ink displays, HDMI sticks, or small touchscreen devices using ESP32 boards or Raspberry Pis.
author: The Verge

title: Research roundup: 6 cool science stories we almost missed
content:
Research roundup: 6 cool science stories we almost missed

A recent research roundup highlights six intriguing science stories that have flown under the radar. Among the featured topics are “Spooky action at the LHC,” investigations into “Ice Age psychoactive use,” and the use of “yeast for building homes on Mars,” along with several other stories.

The collection showcases a diverse range of scientific inquiries, from particle physics experiments at the Large Hadron Collider to studies of ancient psychoactive practices and innovative applications of yeast in extraterrestrial construction. The roundup aims to bring attention to these lesser‑known but captivating research efforts.
summary: Also: Spooky action at the LHC, Ice Age psychoactive use, yeast for building homes on Mars, and more.
author: Ars Technica

title: US arrests tech CEO over $300M Nvidia chip smuggling into China
content:
The United States has arrested a technology chief who is accused of smuggling $300 million worth of Nvidia chips into China. The arrest is part of a broader effort to curb the illicit transfer of advanced semiconductor technology.

Nvidia’s chip‑smuggling problem, according to officials, will not disappear as additional arrests continue to target individuals involved in the illegal trade.
summary: The US has arrested a tech CEO accused of smuggling $300 million in Nvidia chips into China. Nvidia says the chip‑smuggling problem won’t go away as arrests continue.
author: Ars Technica

title: 2008 Crisis Led US to Decouple Carbon Emissions from GDP Growth
content:
The 2008 economic crisis changed the US's relationship with energy  

It wasn't obvious at the time, but the US uncoupled carbon emissions and GDP growth.  

The 2008 economic crisis marked a turning point in the United States' energy and environmental trajectory, as the country was able to separate economic expansion from increases in carbon emissions.
summary: The 2008 economic crisis changed the US's relationship with energy. The US decoupled carbon emissions from GDP growth.
author: Ars Technica

title: Patient-zero drill finds 40% of 73 health facilities fail test
content:
A patient‑zero drill was conducted to test the readiness of healthcare facilities, and the results revealed that 40 % of the sites did not meet the required standards.  

In the exercise, actors wearing makeup and displaying fabricated symptoms entered 73 healthcare facilities, simulating a real outbreak scenario.
summary: Actors with makeup and fake symptoms staggered into 73 healthcare facilities. The drill showed that 40% of the facilities failed the test.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon's $1B data center backlash plan draws more criticism
content:
Amazon’s $1B plan to combat data center backlash draws more backlash. The initiative, aimed at addressing concerns over Amazon’s data center operations, has sparked renewed criticism from environmental and industry observers.

Amazon was praised for ending non‑disclosure agreements that had previously limited public discussion of its data center practices. However, the company has been slammed for downplaying the pollution generated by its data centers, a point that has intensified the backlash.

The criticism highlights a tension between Amazon’s efforts to improve transparency and its ongoing environmental impact.
summary: Amazon's $1B plan to address data center backlash has drawn additional criticism. Amazon was praised for ending NDAs but was slammed for downplaying data center pollution.
author: Ars Technica

title: Circuit Breaker Labs develops crash-test dummies to improve AI safety
content:
Circuit Breaker Labs hopes to make AI safer for your kids (and you).  The company points out that while much discussion centers on AI’s potential to cause catastrophic harm, the technology has already inflicted psychological damage on some people.

In response, Circuit Breaker Labs has created “crash‑test dummies” to address that issue.
summary: Circuit Breaker Labs has created "crash-test dummies" to address psychological harm caused by AI. The company hopes to make AI safer for kids and adults.
author: TechCrunch

title: White House gathers top CEOs, Trump signs order renaming AI “super intelligence”
content:
The White House convened a meeting with several leading technology executives, including Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, to sign an artificial‑intelligence safety pledge that President Donald Trump described as “morally binding.”  

President Trump also signed an executive order that formally rebrands artificial intelligence as “super intelligence.”  

In parallel, Meta and OpenAI are redesigning the public presentation of their AI products.
summary: The White House convened major tech CEOs—including Zuckerberg, Bezos, Musk and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei—to sign an AI safety pledge that President Donald Trump called “morally binding.” Trump also signed an executive order officially rebranding AI as “super intelligence,” while Meta and OpenAI are adopting friendlier branding for their AI products.
author: TechCrunch

title: Apple to tighten macOS Full Disk Access controls amid AI agent risks
content:
Apple announced that it will introduce additional controls for macOS’s Full Disk Access permission. The company said the move is prompted by the growing capabilities of AI agents, which it warns increase the risk associated with broad access to users’ files, messages, mail and browsing history.

The new controls are intended to limit how AI-driven software can obtain such data, aiming to protect user privacy as AI agents become more capable. Apple’s statement underscores its focus on tightening security measures in response to these emerging threats.
summary: Apple announced it will add new controls around macOS’s Full Disk Access permission. The company warned that increasingly capable AI agents make broad access to users’ files, messages, mail and browsing history riskier.
author: TechCrunch

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Expo+ Pass offered for $75 to first 100 qualifiers
content:
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is offering an Expo+ Pass for $75, aimed at individuals who may have been affected by recent layoffs. The promotion is limited to the first 100 qualifying participants.

Interested parties can secure the discounted pass by acting quickly, as only the initial 100 eligible applicants will receive the offer.
summary: The Expo+ Pass for TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 is available for $75. The deal is limited to the first 100 qualifying people.
author: TechCrunch

title: Sean Parker rebuilds Stability AI around music with label support
content:
Sean Parker is rebuilding Stability AI with a focus on music, according to the announcement.

The tech entrepreneur, who previously taught the music industry “what asking for forgiveness looks like,” is now moving forward with the backing and financing of record labels.
summary: Sean Parker is rebuilding Stability AI around music. He is back with the labels' blessing and money.
author: TechCrunch

title: Georgia Holds Emergency Meeting Over AI Threat to Voter Privacy
content:
Georgia has convened an emergency meeting to discuss the possibility that artificial intelligence could expose voters’ secret ballots.  

A Princeton researcher has shown that publicly available election records can be combined with AI to link individual voters to the ballots they cast. The research highlights that, while voters’ choices are intended to remain confidential from family, neighbors, and the government, AI techniques could potentially reveal those votes.  

The meeting will address the implications of this capability for voter privacy and election integrity.
summary: A Princeton researcher discovered that publicly available election records can be combined with AI to link voters to their ballots. Georgia held an emergency meeting to address the potential exposure of secret votes.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Argentina proposes 'golden passport' for foreign cash or bond investment
content:
Argentina announced on Friday that it will offer citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for cash contributions or investments in government bonds. The move is part of a new “golden passport” scheme aimed at attracting foreign capital.  

The initiative comes as libertarian President Javier Milei seeks new sources of dollars to address the country’s debt burden. Milei’s administration has highlighted the need for additional foreign investment to support Argentina’s fiscal situation.  

The program will allow foreign investors to obtain Argentine citizenship through the specified financial contributions, according to the government announcement.
summary: Argentina announced on Friday plans to offer citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for cash contributions or investments in government bonds. President Javier Milei is seeking new sources of dollars for the debt‑burdened nation.
author: Euronews

title: US suspends consular services in Brazil amid Lula and Bolsonaro election race
content:
The United States and Australia suspended consular services in Brazil on Friday amid security concerns, according to reports.  

President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his rival, Flavio Bolsonaro, are engaging in a last‑ditch effort to win voters ahead of Sunday’s election in Brazil.  

The suspension of consular services came as the two candidates intensified their campaigns, with both leaders “pulling no punches” in the final days before the vote.
summary: The United States and Australia suspended consular services in Brazil on Friday because of security concerns. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and rival Flavio Bolsonaro are intensifying their campaigns ahead of Sunday's election.
author: Euronews

title: Spanish parliament rejects two affordable housing bills, dealing blow to Sanchez government
content:
Spanish lawmakers rejected two affordable housing bills on Friday, a setback for Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s government.

The bills were introduced by the government in an attempt to address the concerns of demonstrators protesting Spain’s housing crisis. The protesters reacted with fury at the parliamentary decision.

Rents in Spain have doubled over the past decade, and average prices are now almost equivalent to the average young person’s monthly salary.
summary: Spain's parliament rejected two affordable‑housing bills that Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez had promoted. Demonstrators protested the decision, noting that rents have doubled in a decade and now cost about a young person’s monthly salary.
author: France 24

title: French school protests erupt in multiple cities, some turning violent
content:
French school protests have spread across the country in the past 18 days, prompting observers to wonder whether the unrest resembles a new “Yellow Vests” movement. The demonstrations began with isolated actions at a high school in Rennes, at a school in Caen and at Villeneuve‑d’Ascq on the outskirts of Lille, where students complained of overloaded timetables, staffing shortages and poor facilities.

The protests quickly expanded to Saint‑Denis and Créteil on the outskirts of Paris, and a student interview posted on TikTok was viewed 1.4 million times. Over the following week the actions multiplied into hundreds of demonstrations, ranging from peaceful rallies to violent scenes that included makeshift barricades, a fire set at a school in Nantes, firefighters forced from a vehicle in Marseille and a fire engine set alight, and an incident in which a female police officer was attacked while youths shouted “kill her.”

The government has described the unrest as urban violence and accused agitators linked to the hard left of exploiting genuine concerns for political ends ahead of the election. La France Insoumise denied that it favours any violent means of action. In a Spotlight segment, teacher Jean Rémi Girard of Asnières‑sur‑Seine, who also serves as president of the National Union des Lycées et Collèges covering education workers from primary schools to colleges (ages 7‑18), discussed the developments.
summary: Students at schools in Rennes, Caen, Villeneueve d'Asque and later Saint Denis, Creteil, Nantes and Marseille staged protests over overloaded timetables, staffing problems and poor facilities, with a TikTok interview of participants viewed 1.4 million times. The demonstrations included both peaceful rallies and violent scenes such as a fire at a Nantes school, a fire engine set alight in Marseille and an attack on a female police officer, prompting the government to blame hard‑left agitators while La France Insoumise denied supporting violence.
author: France 24

title: Joseph Kony remains at large as LRA attacks eastern Central African Republic
content:
Recent attacks in the eastern Central African Republic have been linked to the Lord’s Resistance Army (LRA), a Ugandan militia notorious for massacres and mass child abductions in the 1990s and 2000s. The incidents, reported over the past several months, indicate a resurgence of the group’s activity in the region.

Joseph Kony, the LRA’s leader, has been wanted by the International Criminal Court for more than 20 years and remains at large. France 24 interviewed Leonie von Braun, the ICC’s lead investigator on the Kony case, who confirmed that Kony is still “active” within the LRA despite his long‑term fugitive status.
summary: In recent months the eastern Central African Republic has suffered several attacks attributed to the Lord’s Resistance Army, a Ugandan militia known for 1990s‑2000s massacres and child abductions. The group’s leader Joseph Kony, wanted by the International Criminal Court for more than 20 years, remains at large, and ICC lead investigator Leonie von Braun discussed the resurgence with FRANCE 24.
author: France 24

title: UN-led dialogue urges collective action to address global information crisis
content:
A UN‑led dialogue highlighted the need for collective action to address a global information crisis, according to the meeting’s summary. Participants emphasized that the rapidly changing information landscape requires stronger cooperation and practical steps.

Governments, UN entities, civil society, media, academia and the private sector all called for coordinated efforts to respond to these challenges.
summary: Governments, UN entities, civil society, media, academia and the private sector called for stronger cooperation and practical action. They seek to respond to a rapidly changing global information landscape.
author: UN News

title: UN rights chief Volker Türk calls Ukraine war a growing human rights catastrophe
content:
UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said the war in Ukraine is a “human rights catastrophe” that is “growing and intensifying by the week.”  

Türk warned on Friday that the conflict threatens an even greater disaster across the region.
summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said the war in Ukraine is a human rights catastrophe. He said on Friday that the situation is growing and intensifying by the week and threatens an even greater disaster across the region.
author: UN News

title: WHO: Global life expectancy nearly returns to pre‑pandemic level
content: The World Health Organization announced on Friday that global life expectancy has almost fully recovered from the disruption caused by the COVID‑19 pandemic. The agency said people around the world are living longer again, with the overall figure now close to pre‑pandemic levels.
summary: The World Health Organization said on Friday that global life expectancy has almost fully recovered from the COVID‑19 pandemic. People around the world are now living longer again.
author: UN News

title: UN steps up aid for 12 neglected crises, stressing need for open roads and borders
content:
The United Nations announced a new push to increase assistance for twelve crises that have received little attention, emphasizing that “money alone won’t get us there.”  

UN officials said delivering aid to people in the world’s most neglected emergencies requires more than funding; it also depends on open roads, open borders and the cooperation of leaders willing to help the assistance reach those in dire need.
summary: The UN is stepping up assistance for twelve of the world’s most neglected emergencies. Officials say delivering aid also requires open roads, open borders and leaders willing to facilitate it.
author: UN News

title: Ethiopia accuses Egypt, Eritrea and Sudan of backing armed groups
content: Addis Ababa has warned that the conflict in Ethiopia could spread regionally, alleging external support for armed groups. The Ethiopian government says Egypt, Eritrea and Sudan are backing these factions. The accusations raise concerns about a broader escalation involving neighboring countries. No further details were provided.
summary: Addis Ababa accuses Egypt, Eritrea and Sudan of backing armed groups. The accusations come as the conflict in Ethiopia is viewed as potentially expanding across the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: California leads lawsuit alleging NHTSA violated mandate on Trump fuel‑efficiency rollback
content:
California is leading a lawsuit challenging the Trump administration’s rollback of fuel‑efficiency standards.  

The complaint alleges that the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has violated its congressional mandate by failing to set fuel‑economy standards at the “maximum feasible” level.  

The case centers on whether the agency’s actions contravene the statutory requirement to achieve the highest practicable fuel‑efficiency outcomes.
summary: California is leading a lawsuit that challenges the Trump fuel efficiency standards rollback. The suit alleges that NHTSA has violated its congressional mandate to set fuel‑economy standards at the maximum feasible level.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iraq approves 40 daily Najaf flights for Iranian airlines after US waiver
content:
Baghdad has approved a schedule of 40 daily flights to Najaf for Iranian airlines after the United States granted a waiver that allowed the arrangement.

Mahan Air was excluded from the agreement, with Iraqi officials saying Washington approved a specific request for a waiver that kept the carrier out of the new flight plan.
summary: Iraq has approved 40 daily flights to Najaf for Iranian airlines following a U.S. exemption. Mahan Air is excluded from the agreement after Washington granted a waiver request.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Latin America sees China as more positive global influence than US, poll shows
content: A recent Latinobarometro poll indicates that public opinion in Latin America is shifting toward a more favorable view of China’s global role while attitudes toward the United States are declining. The annual survey, which gauges attitudes across the region, found that perceptions of China’s influence have improved, whereas views of U.S. influence have worsened. The results suggest a growing preference for China over the United States among Latin American respondents.
summary: The annual Latinobarometro survey reports that Latin Americans view China’s global influence more positively than that of the United States. The survey finds perceptions of China’s influence improving while views of U.S. influence are worsening.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Christa Pike unconscious on ventilator after botched execution, lawyers say
content:
Christa Pike, a Tennessee woman, is reported to be unconscious and on a ventilator following what her lawyers describe as a botched execution. The legal team said the incident occurred after an attempt to administer the lethal drug.

The attorneys added that doctors are currently working to clear doses of the drug pentobarbital from Pike’s system.
summary: Christa Pike is unconscious and on a ventilator following a botched execution. Her legal team says doctors are working to clear pentobarbital from her system.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Jon Watts to Direct New Star Wars Trilogy Continuing Skywalker Saga
content:
Deadline reports that Lucasfilm has hired director Jon Watts to lead the first installment of a new trilogy intended to continue the Skywalker saga, with screenwriter Simon Kinberg attached to the project. Daisy Ridley is reportedly being considered to reprise her role as Rey, although the films have not yet been greenlit and few other details have been confirmed.

The article critiques the decision to return to the Skywalker family, describing the clan as having already shaped the galaxy through decades of cyclic conflicts involving Death Stars, Jedi orders, and dark side turnarounds. It suggests that while Star Wars has previously explored other corners of the galaxy through characters like smugglers and bounty hunters, the franchise has struggled to move away from the central family dynamic.

The piece notes that Watts, who directed Spider-Man: No Way Home, is seen as an inspired choice for the role, particularly given that his previous work centered on the concept of characters in long-running franchises not remaining dead. The author argues that relying on the same family saga is a waste of time, expressing a desire for newer worlds within the Star Wars universe.
summary: Deadline reports that Lucasfilm has hired Jon Watts to direct a new trilogy continuing the Skywalker saga, which is written by Simon Kinberg. Daisy Ridley is reportedly being considered to return as Rey, though the films have not yet been greenlit.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Bassam Tariq's Houston-set thriller stars Mahershala Ali as a Muslim hitman
content:
Mahershala Ali stars as Latif, a devout Muslim and contract killer, in the Houston-set thriller Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, written and directed by Bassam Tariq. In the film, Latif fashions himself a righteous killer who justifies his violence as divine retribution against those he believes have offended God. According to Tariq, the character’s use of a sword is a central part of his code and a negotiation with his faith, with Tariq noting that using a sword forces one to strike with intention.

Tariq discussed the film in a recent interview in Toronto, where he reflected on his career pivot from a stalled reboot of Marvel’s Blade to this new project. The director stated, “I’m happier I made this movie,” indicating his satisfaction with the shift in focus to Ali’s thriller.
summary: Mahershala Ali stars as Latif, a devout Muslim who works as a contract killer in Bassam Tariq's Houston-set film. Tariq explains that the character's use of a sword is part of his code and a negotiation with his faith.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Seth Meyers mocks Trump's use of taxpayer funds for campaign ads
content:
Late-night hosts addressed Donald Trump’s use of taxpayer funds to finance campaign advertisements, a practice that has led Republican midterm candidates to distance themselves from the former president. The comedians focused on the unpopularity of Trump among these GOP candidates and his insistence that US taxpayers bear the cost of recycled campaign ads.

Seth Meyers specifically questioned the financial burden placed on the public, asking, “Is there anything this grub won’t make us pay for?”
summary: Late-night hosts discussed Donald Trump's use of taxpayer money to fund recycled campaign ads. They also addressed his unpopularity with GOP midterm candidates who are distancing themselves from him.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Dolly Parton sings Jolene in Welsh in posthumous recording
content: Dolly Parton’s niece Jada Star and Welsh singer Bronwen Lewis have announced that the country artist was proud to sing in Welsh. This statement accompanies the release of a recording in which Parton performs the song "Jolene" in the Welsh language.
summary: A recording of Dolly Parton singing Jolene in Welsh was released after her death. Her niece Jada Star and Welsh singer Bronwen Lewis stated that Parton was proud to sing in Welsh.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: K-pop giants Stray Kids join BTS in boycotting the Grammys
content: K-pop group Stray Kids have joined BTS in boycotting the Grammy Awards, becoming the second major act to withdraw from the ceremony. The decision by both groups is a response to the introduction of a new best Asian Pop award category.
summary: Stray Kids become the second major act to withdraw from the Grammys over the new best Asian Pop award.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Alison Hammond has hospital heart check-up after leaving This Morning
content: Alison Hammond underwent a heart check-up in a hospital after departing midway through the broadcast of the television show This Morning on Friday. The host stated that she is currently "fine" but is undergoing the medical assessment following her early exit from the program.
summary: Alison Hammond is undergoing a heart check-up in the hospital after leaving midway through Friday's This Morning. The host stated that she is fine but is getting checked.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Emmanuel Iyogun on his journey from reluctant prop to England debut
content:
Emmanuel Iyogun, the Northampton star and Spain-born son of Nigerian immigrants, earned his England debut off the bench in Argentina in July after a career defined by resilience. Head coach Steve Borthwick selected the prop for the match, marking a significant milestone in Iyogun’s unlikely journey to the international ranks.

Iyogun credits his parents’ advice for his determination, noting that he was always told he would have to work harder than others and might not receive initial privileges. This mindset led him to persist whenever he was told no or faced obstacles, viewing continued hard work as the only response. The article also highlights his recent interaction with Springbok forward Ox Nché, with whom he shared “massive cakes.”
summary: Emmanuel Iyogun, a Spain-born son of Nigerian immigrants, earned his England debut off the bench in Argentina in July. The Northampton star described his rise as requiring immense determination and resilience, noting that his parents always told him he would have to work harder than others.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wakey-Wakey: Trinity’s rapid rise and Grand Final run shocks fans from long slumber
content:
Wakefield Trinity will face Warrington in their maiden Super League Grand Final on Saturday, an event expected to draw more than 70,000 supporters. The club’s rapid ascent stands in stark contrast to its status 965 days prior, when it played a match in Siddal, on the outskirts of Halifax, in front of only a few hundred spectators.

The transformation followed a takeover completed in late 2023 by boyhood Wakefield Trinity fan Matt Ellis, who has since injected £10m worth of investment into the organization. This financial commitment has led to visible results both on and off the field, propelling the club from a state described as a “shambles” to becoming a headline attraction in the sport.
summary: Club was a ‘shambles’ before takeover by boyhood Wakefield fan Matt Ellis – and on Saturday they face Warrington for the titleLast one out of Wakefield on Saturday, turn off the lights. Some 965 days ago, this story began on a field in Siddal on the outskirts of Halifax with just a few hundred people there to see it: this weekend, one of rugby league’s grand old clubs will be the headline attraction in front of more than 70,000 supporters when Trinity face Warrington in their maiden Super League Grand Final.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe: Waud seeks Hollywood ending after Snakes on a Plane
content:
Film producer George Waud, who spent 23 years in Los Angeles and recently served as a co-producer on the London West End revival of Cabaret, is the owner of Maltese Cross, the second favorite in the upcoming Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe. Waud acknowledged this week that he is not a typical owner for the most prestigious and valuable race of the European season, stating that he is making the most of the opportunity.

The horse’s journey to the Bois de Boulogne for the first Sunday in October includes a backstory rooted in Waud’s early life. Racing has been a consistent thread in his life since he took a trip to Newmarket with his mother in the 1970s. Maltese Cross will compete against runners from racing’s superpowers in the event.
summary: Film producer is certainly not a typical owner of the second favourite for the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe with Maltese Cross part of a remarkable scriptAs George Waud is the first to concede, he is not a typical owner of the second favourite for the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe. “No,” he said this week, three days out from the most prestigious and valuable race of the European season, when his colt Maltese Cross will take on runners from racing’s superpowers.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Mercedes team first as Russell and Antonelli face off at Sepang
content:
Mercedes has prioritized team strategy as title rivals George Russell and Andrea Kimi Antonelli prepare to face off during Formula One’s return to Malaysia. The event, officially designated as the “Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia,” marks the sport’s first visit to the Sepang circuit since 2017. Both drivers are bringing upgrades to the demanding track, which is known for its high temperatures and humidity that present a significant physical challenge.

The championship battle is further complicated by a resurgence from Red Bull, with Max Verstappen determined to make his mark on the title run-in. Despite the unusual naming convention that may puzzle statisticians, the focus remains on the competitive dynamics at the sharp end of the grid. The return to the much-liked Sepang circuit has been welcomed within the sport, setting the stage for a pivotal weekend in the season.
summary: Title rivals Russell and Antonelli bring upgrades to the first Grand Prix in Malaysia since 2017. The race is held at the demanding Sepang circuit, which is known for high temperatures and humidity.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lib Dems urge Andy Burnham to reveal Manchester City owner meetings
content: Liberal Democrats have urged Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham to disclose details of all meetings held with Manchester City’s owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), and to declare any hospitality accepted at the Etihad Stadium. This call follows criticism of Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, who stated this week that he would be “really concerned” if ADUG were forced to sell the club after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations. The prime minister’s comments prompted Downing Street to issue two clarifications of his position on Thursday.
summary: The Liberal Democrats are calling for Andy Burnham to publish details of all meetings with Manchester City's owners and declare accepted hospitality. This follows criticism of the Prime Minister for expressing concern if the Abu Dhabi United Group were forced to sell the club.
author: Guardian Sport

title: If America wants to prosper, we must lead
content: Sen. Rick Scott and Hudson Institute Fellow Rebeccah Heinrichs argue that the United States must maintain its role as a global leader to counter an emerging authoritarian alliance led by China and Russia. They contend that American prosperity is directly tied to its ability to lead on the international stage.
summary: Sen. Rick Scott and Hudson Institute Fellow Rebeccah Heinrichs argue that the United States must maintain global leadership to counter an emerging authoritarian alliance led by China and Russia.

title: Hegseth orders US troops 1 day off to vote in October
content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced on Friday that all U.S. troops will receive one day off in October to vote in the 2026 midterm elections. The stand-down order is scheduled to be executed on October 15.

Hegseth stated that this policy will continue in even-numbered election years as part of a new and “apolitical” Pentagon.
summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that all U.S. Troops will receive one day off in October to vote in the 2026 midterm elections. The stand-down order is set for Oct. 15 and will continue in even-numbered election years.
author: The Hill

title: Trump motorcade neared 100 mph driving from Texas to Oklahoma due to storms
content: President Trump’s motorcade reached speeds approaching 100 mph on Thursday as the president drove from a rally in Texas to Oklahoma, opting for ground transportation after stormy weather in the South ruled out the use of a helicopter or airplane. The high-speed drive took place during the president’s travel from an event at the Peterbilt Motors manufacturing plant in Denton, Texas, to a second scheduled event in Durant, Oklahoma.
summary: President Trump drove from a rally in Denton, Texas, to Durant, Oklahoma, because stormy weather ruled out helicopter and airplane travel. His motorcade reached speeds near 100 mph during the journey.
author: The Hill

title: Tories prepare for election with focus on economy and welfare
content:
Kemi Badenoch has instructed her team to prepare for a possible early election as the Conservative Party aims to be election-ready ahead of its upcoming party conference. The leadership is emphasizing a strategic focus on key policy areas to position the party for potential immediate electoral challenges.

The party’s preparations will center on the economy and welfare, with Badenoch directing her team to prioritize these issues in their planning. This approach reflects an effort to ensure the Conservatives are fully prepared to campaign on these specific platforms should an early election be called.
summary: Kemi Badenoch has instructed her team to prepare for a possible early election. The party will prioritize the economy and welfare ahead of its conference.
author: BBC Politics

title: Big banks in net zero alliance continued lending to coal firms
content: New data indicates that global coal finance has remained steady since 2022, a trend observed as international efforts to reduce the connection between lending and emissions have waned. The findings highlight that major banks participating in the “net zero” alliance have continued to extend loans to coal companies.
summary: New data indicates that coal finance has remained steady globally since 2022. This trend occurred as international efforts to reduce the link between lending and emissions faded.
author: Climate Home News

title: The Colorado River is shrinking. What happens next?
content:
Lake Mead, located in Nevada, has reached its lowest level since being filled nearly 90 years ago, while Lake Powell is also at a historic low. During a tour of the reservoir, Colby Pellegrino of the Southern Nevada Water Authority pointed out a large metal pipe protruding from a rock island, a feature that had previously been submerged.

Pellegrino identified the pipe as the first intake constructed in 1970 to deliver municipal water to the valley. The exposure of this infrastructure highlights the significant drop in water levels, which occurred during a visit when temperatures reached 42C (108F).
summary: Lake Mead is at its lowest level since it was filled nearly 90 years ago, Lake Powell also at a historic lowIt was 42C (108F) degrees as we motored across Nevada’s Lake Mead in our rented pontoon boat. Colby Pellegrino with the Southern Nevada Water Authority wanted to show us something we shouldn’t have been able to see.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Stem cell-derived brain models offer new window into anesthesia mechanisms
content: Hundreds of thousands of people undergo general anesthesia daily, relying on the procedure to safely induce unconsciousness during surgery. Despite decades of clinical use, the precise mechanisms by which anesthetic drugs alter the brain's electrical activity to produce this state remain incompletely understood by scientists.
summary: Scientists are using stem cell-derived brain models to investigate how anesthetic drugs reshape the brain's electrical activity to produce unconsciousness. This research aims to address the lack of understanding regarding how these drugs work, despite general anesthesia being used on hundreds of thousands of people daily.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UTSW study shows greater blood protein variability in MS patients using generic drugs
content:
A study led by researchers at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center (UTSW) indicates that generic versions of three commonly prescribed oral multiple sclerosis (MS) therapies may result in different biological outcomes compared to brand-name drugs. The research focused on patients taking these oral medications and measured blood proteins linked to MS disease activity.

The findings revealed that patients using the generic versions of the drugs exhibited greater variability in these blood protein markers than those taking the brand-name versions. This suggests that the generic formulations may produce less consistent effects on disease activity indicators in the bloodstream.
summary: UTSW researchers found that MS patients taking generic versions of three commonly prescribed oral therapies had greater variability in blood proteins associated with MS disease activity. Patients taking brand-name versions of those drugs had less variability in those proteins.
author: Medical Xpress

title: US pharmacy closures disproportionately affect racial minority communities
content:
Pharmacies across the United States are shutting down at a rapid pace, creating “pharmacy deserts” that leave millions of Americans without convenient access to essential health services. Research shows that nearly one in three pharmacies closed between 2010 and 2021, and more than 7,000 pharmacies have closed since 2019.

The surge in closures is disproportionately impacting racial minority communities, intensifying disparities in access to medication and health care. These communities now face heightened challenges in obtaining timely pharmacy services.

The continued loss of pharmacy locations threatens the health infrastructure of affected neighborhoods, underscoring the need for targeted interventions to address the growing gap in care.
summary: Pharmacies across the United States are closing rapidly, creating pharmacy deserts that leave millions without convenient access to care, and the closures are hitting racial minority communities the hardest. Research shows nearly one in three pharmacies closed between 2010 and 2021, including over 7,000 closures since 2019.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Lab-grown mini-bladder explains recurring urinary tract infections
content: Research into lab-grown "mini-bladders" is helping scientists understand why urinary tract infections (UTIs) frequently recur after initial treatment. For many individuals, the symptoms of a UTI, such as burning and frequent urination, disappear once antibiotics are finished but often return weeks or months later.
summary: Urinary tract infections often return weeks or months after antibiotics end. A lab-grown mini-bladder helps explain why these recurring infections happen.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Hidden lymphatic signal amplifier could inform treatments for lymphedema and cancer metastasis
content: Lymphatic vessels function as the body's drainage system by collecting excess fluid from tissues. When these vessels are underdeveloped, damaged, or dysfunctional, lymphatic drainage is impaired, leading to the development of lymphedema. This condition results in swelling that particularly affects the arms and legs.
summary: Lymphatic vessels function as the body's drainage system by collecting excess fluid from tissues. Impaired lymphatic drainage due to underdeveloped, damaged, or dysfunctional vessels can cause lymphedema, resulting in swelling in the arms and legs.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Ohio State study: Comparing past selves harms well-being
content:
A new study from The Ohio State University highlights that individuals often serve as their own harshest critics when evaluating their body image. The research indicates that people frequently compare their current selves to past versions, a process that can significantly impact their well-being.

This finding shifts focus from the traditional body image research, which has for decades concentrated almost exclusively on social comparisons and their toll on mental health. The Ohio State University study reveals that internal comparisons with one's own history are a critical factor in how individuals perceive their bodies.
summary: A new study from The Ohio State University indicates that comparing current selves with past versions is a major source of negative self-criticism. This finding contrasts with decades of body image research that focused primarily on social comparisons.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Ford retains No. 3 U.S. sales spot in Q3 despite 6.6% decline
content:
Ford reported a year-over-year sales decline of 6.6% during the third quarter, selling 507,395 light-duty vehicles. The automaker announced the figures on Friday.

Despite the drop in sales, Ford retained the No. 3 position in U.S. sales, fending off Hyundai.
summary: Ford reported a year-over-year sales decline of 6.6% during the third quarter. The company sold 507,395 light-duty vehicles while retaining the No. 3 U.S. sales position.
author: CNBC Business

title: G7 to release up to 100m barrels of emergency oil and diesel reserves
content:
Leaders of G7 nations have agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency diesel and crude oil stockpiles in response to surging fuel prices. The decision follows pressure from Donald Trump to ease the impact of rising costs on households and economies.

The coordinated drawdown of reserves from some of the world’s largest economies will be managed by the International Energy Agency (IEA). According to French President Emmanuel Macron, the release of the oil and diesel is scheduled to take place within four months.
summary: G7 leaders agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency diesel and crude oil stockpiles within four months. The coordinated drawdown, managed by the International Energy Agency, aims to ease surging fuel prices and pressure on economies.
author: Guardian Business

title: US adds 29,000 jobs in September as unemployment rises to 4.2%
content:
US employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, a sharp decline from previous monthly gains, while the unemployment rate rose slightly to 4.2%. This final jobs report before the midterm elections indicated a cooling labor market, with the figures falling to less than half of economists’ expectations for just under 70,000 new positions.

According to data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, most job gains were concentrated in the healthcare industry, which added 17,000 new jobs. Conversely, the information, financial, and professional industries experienced job losses during the period.
summary: US employers added 29,000 jobs in September, a figure under half of economists' expectations, while the unemployment rate rose slightly to 4.2%. Most job gains were concentrated in the healthcare industry, which added 17,000 new jobs, while the information, financial, and professional industries saw losses.
author: Guardian Business

title: Scotland Supermarkets Face New Rules on High Sugar, Fat, and Salt Products
content: New regulations in Scotland are set to restrict the placement of products high in sugar, fat, and salt within supermarkets. These measures aim to limit the visibility and accessibility of such items to consumers. Despite these changes to product placement, the meal deal remains available.
summary: Restrictions are being implemented in Scottish supermarkets to limit products with high sugar, fat, and salt content. Despite these new rules, the meal deal will continue to be available.
author: BBC Business

title: US Jobs Market Slows Ahead of Midterm Elections
content:
The U.S. jobs market experienced a sharp slowdown as American employers paused hiring activities. This shift in the labor landscape occurred with the midterm elections just one month away.

During this period, the unemployment rate rose slightly, reflecting the broader pause in new employment across the country.
summary: Unemployment rose slightly as American employers paused hiring. This slowdown occurred with midterm elections just a month away.
author: BBC Business

title: Multilingual readers report higher enjoyment and more daily reading, survey finds
content: The U.K.’s National Year of Reading is encouraging people across the country to “go all in” on reading. This initiative has prompted discussions among families regarding what to read, which language to use, and what form the reading should take.
summary: A survey found that multilingual readers report higher enjoyment of reading. The U. K.'s National Year of Reading encourages people to read more, but families are unsure what to read, in which language, and in what form.
author: Phys.org

title: New research shows how water would behave on the moon
content:
New research shows how water would behave on the moon.

As humanity looks toward future bases on the moon, plant cultivation will be critical for sustaining life there.

Plants can provide food, oxygen, medicine, water purification and waste recycling, making them indispensable for lunar development.
summary: Humanity looks toward future bases on the moon, and plant cultivation will be critical for sustaining life there. Plants can provide food, oxygen, medicine, water purification and waste recycling, making them indispensable for lunar development.
author: Phys.org

title: Red squirrels endangered in Britain as range shrinks, says expert
content:
Red squirrels, once common across Britain, have largely vanished from much of their former range.  

Dr. Kat Hamill, senior lecturer in zoology at Nottingham Trent University, explains the factors behind the decline of this native mammal and discusses whether scientific research and conservation efforts can help restore its population.
summary: The red squirrel, once a familiar sight across Britain, has disappeared from much of its former range. Dr. Kat Hamill, senior lecturer in zoology at Nottingham Trent University, explains the causes and whether science and conservation can help restore the species.
author: Phys.org

title: CHARA Array Finds Infrared Edge Darkening Gaps in Stellar Models
content:
Astronomers using Georgia State University's Center for High Angular Resolution Astronomy (CHARA) Array have discovered that nearby stars darken more strongly toward their edges at near‑infrared wavelengths than current stellar atmosphere models predict.

The study shows that the limb‑darkening effect is stronger in the near‑infrared than the widely used models anticipate, exposing gaps in the theoretical description of how stars distribute their light.

These observations provide a new benchmark for understanding the structure of stars and the accuracy of existing stellar atmosphere models.
summary: Astronomers using Georgia State University's Center for High Angular Resolution Astronomy (CHARA) Array found that nearby stars darken toward their edges more strongly at near-infrared wavelengths than predicted by several widely used models of stellar atmospheres. This finding provides a new benchmark for understanding how stars are structured.
author: Phys.org

title: KIT researchers develop enzyme beads for greener chemical production
content:
Researchers at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) have created a method to assemble enzymes into millimeter‑sized beads that can be stored and used as biocatalysts. In the new technology, the enzymes serve both as the catalytic agents and as the structural material of the beads.

A variant of the approach allows the enzyme networks within the beads to be combined with living cells, expanding potential applications. The team has filed a patent application for the technology, and the findings were published in the journal Advanced Materials.
summary: Researchers at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology have developed a method to assemble enzymes into millimeter‑sized, storable beads that act as both catalyst and structural material. A variant combines the enzyme networks with living cells, a patent application has been filed, and the work was published in Advanced Materials.
author: Phys.org

title: Patriot Front White Nationalists March in Washington on July 4
content:
In the lead-up to the nation's 250th birthday on July 4, images of a large demonstration in Washington circulated on television and social media. Hundreds of masked men marched through the streets carrying flags and chanting "Reclaim America!"

The marchers were identified as members of Patriot Front, a white nationalist group, based on logos displayed on their identical baseball caps.
summary: Hundreds of masked men marched through Washington carrying flags and chanting “Reclaim America!” The marchers were identified as members of Patriot Front, a white nationalist group.
author: Phys.org

title: Study Finds First Week of Life Crucial for Future Allergy and Eczema Risk
content: A recent study involving hundreds of infants challenges the prevailing scientific consensus that the immune system develops without distinct critical phases. The research indicates that the first week of an infant's life is a crucial period that significantly influences future health outcomes, specifically regarding the risk of developing allergies and eczema.
summary: The mainstream view holds that there are no critical phases in immune system development. A study of hundreds of infants indicates that the first week of life may be crucial for future allergy and eczema risk.
author: New Scientist

title: Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over truth in math solutions
content:
AI models are solving mathematics problems at an increasing pace, with a technique known as formalisation serving as the key method for demonstrating the correctness of their claimed solutions. This process has sparked a behind-the-scenes battle among mathematicians and AI systems regarding the nature of mathematical truth.

The central question facing the field is whether the formalisation process itself can be trusted to accurately verify these AI-generated solutions.
summary: AI models are solving mathematics problems at an increasing pace. A formalisation technique is key to proving the correctness of their claimed solutions, but its reliability is in question.
author: New Scientist

title: Fossil mammal with reptile-like teeth shows lifelong tooth replacement
content:
An ancient mammal species from the Cretaceous period, discovered in China, challenges existing understanding of mammalian evolution due to its unique dental capabilities. Unlike most modern mammals, which develop only two sets of teeth during their lifetime, this fossil species appears to have possessed the ability to replace its teeth continuously throughout its life.

The discovery highlights a significant deviation from standard mammalian traits, as the animal retained a reptile-like characteristic in its dentition. This finding provides new insights into the evolutionary history of mammals, suggesting that the transition to a two-set dental system occurred later than previously thought for some lineages.
summary: An ancient Cretaceous species found in China can replace its teeth throughout its life. This lifelong tooth replacement differs from most modern mammals, which only get two sets of teeth.
author: New Scientist

title: NASA Opens Applications for Next Class of Flight Directors
content:
NASA has opened applications for the next class of flight directors, a highly respected role in human spaceflight. The position will be based in mission control at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas.  

Flight directors are essential to NASA’s mission of advancing American leadership in space exploration, particularly as the agency works toward a sustained human presence on the Moon. The role involves leading teams that manage spacecraft operations and mission-critical decisions.  

Applicants can apply now for the upcoming class of flight directors.
summary: NASA is seeking leaders for the flight director position in mission control at its Johnson Space Center in Houston, a role critical to advancing American leadership in space exploration and paving the way for a sustained human presence on the Moon. Applications are being accepted for the next class of flight directors.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Langley Conducts First Unsteady Pressure Sensitive Paint Tests in Transonic Dynamics Tunnel
content:
Researchers at NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, conducted groundbreaking tests to develop new wind tunnel capabilities for future aircraft design. The experiments took place in the center’s Transonic Dynamics Tunnel, marking a significant step in advancing aerodynamic research.

In a first-of-its-kind test, the research team utilized unsteady Pressure Sensitive Paint to analyze how air flows around a standard wind tunnel model. This innovative approach allows for detailed observation of aerodynamic forces during testing.
summary: Researchers at NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, used unsteady Pressure Sensitive Paint to study air flow around a standard wind tunnel model. This first-of-its-kind test in the Transonic Dynamics Tunnel is paving the way for new wind tunnel capabilities for designing future aircraft technologies.
author: NASA News

title: NASA abre solicitudes para próxima promoción de directores de vuelo
content:
La NASA ha abierto las solicitudes para la próxima promoción de directores de vuelo, un puesto considerado uno de los más prestigiosos en el ámbito de los vuelos espaciales tripulados. Estos profesionales se desempeñarán en el control de misión del Centro Espacial Johnson, ubicado en Houston.

La agencia destaca que esta función es fundamental para reforzar el liderazgo dentro de sus operaciones espaciales.
summary: La NASA busca líderes para el puesto de director de vuelo en el control de misión del Centro Espacial Johnson de Houston. Esta función es fundamental para reforzar el liderazgo en el ámbito de los vuelos espaciales tripulados.

content: A Redditor purchased a used central processing unit (CPU) that was subsequently discovered to be banned on the game Valorant. content:

content:

content:

title: Fi Mini and Tractive Cat Trackers Compared: Trade-Offs Highlighted in 2026 Review
content:
In a recent review of smart cat trackers, the author compared the Fi Mini and Tractive models. The evaluation focused on the devices’ performance over several months of monitoring a cat named Basil, tracking both activity and sleep patterns.

After months of monitoring Basil’s activity and sleep, the author found that Fi and Tractive cat trackers come with their own trade‑offs.
summary: The author monitored Basil’s activity and sleep for several months using Fi and Tractive cat trackers. The review notes that each tracker has its own trade-offs.
