title: Amazon stops using NDAs with county officials for data center projects
content:
Amazon announced that it will no longer use nondisclosure agreements, described as secret agreements, with county officials for its data‑center projects. The change comes as the company acknowledges growing community opposition.

Amazon said the backlash has contributed to the emergence of data‑center moratoriums in various locations across the United States.
summary: Amazon announced it has ended the use of NDAs with county officials for its data centers. The company said community backlash is prompting data center moratoriums across the country.
author: Wired

title: Trump’s AI Rebrand Tested Tech Exec Loyalty—and It Worked
content: Billionaires who had previously expressed intense enthusiasm for artificial intelligence complied with Donald Trump’s decision to cancel the term, effectively passing a loyalty test for tech executives. These industry leaders shifted their public stance to align with the president’s rebranding efforts, despite their prior obsession with the technology.
summary: Billionaires had promoted AI for years, yet they complied when Trump cancelled the term. The rebrand tested their loyalty and succeeded.
author: Wired

title: Trillium Labs Plans to Publicly Showcase Self-Improvement Research
content: Trillium Labs intends to conduct high-stakes research on self-improvement and model behavior in a transparent manner, contrasting with many frontier labs that keep similar risky research locked away. The organization aims to publicly showcase its work in these specific areas.
summary: Many frontier labs keep their risky research locked away. Trillium Labs wants to show off its work on self-improvement and model behavior.
author: Wired

title: Home Assistant Renames Cloud Service to Home Assistant Link, Drops Cloud from Logo
content:
Home Assistant, an open-source smart home platform, is renaming its cloud service to Home Assistant Link and removing the cloud from its logo. Founder Paulus Schoutsen told The Verge, “We are renaming Home Assistant Cloud to Home Assistant Link, because we hate clouds,” adding, “Big tech ruined the cloud, so we're out.”

The rebranding is part of a long-term strategy by Schoutsen and his team to establish Home Assistant as a mainstream smart home platform. Schoutsen noted that most users discover the powerful platform after reaching the limits of mainstream options such as Google Home, Amazon Alexa, and Apple Home. He acknowledged that the platform has a steep learning curve.
summary: Home Assistant is renaming its cloud service to Home Assistant Link and removing the cloud from its logo. Founder Paulus Schoutsen said the change reflects the company's dislike of cloud services, citing that big tech ruined the cloud.
author: The Verge

title: Tesla Q3 production rises 3.8% but sales fall year-over-year
content:
Tesla reported that it produced a total of 464,391 vehicles during the third quarter of this year, marking a 3.8 percent increase compared to the same period in 2025. The production figures included 457,387 Model 3 and Model Y units, along with 7,004 "other vehicles" such as the Cybertruck, Cybercab, and Tesla Semi. The company noted that it had discontinued the Model S and X earlier this year.

Although Tesla sold fewer vehicles in the third quarter than it did a year ago, when consumers rushed to utilize expiring federal tax credits for electric vehicle purchases, the company still exceeded Wall Street estimates. These results suggest that Tesla’s recovery remains on track despite the year-over-year sales decline.
summary: Tesla produced 464,391 vehicles in the third quarter, a 3.8 percent increase from the same period in 2025. The company sold fewer vehicles than a year ago when consumers used expiring federal tax credits, but still beat Wall Street estimates.
author: The Verge

title: Paramount’s Warner Bros. megamerger will just be called Skydance
content:
Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison announced that the company will be rebranded as Skydance upon the completion of its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery next week. In a post on X, Ellison stated that the new name was chosen to provide the combined entity with its own identity while keeping the Paramount and Warner Bros. brands in the spotlight.

The merger is set to close after a judge earlier this week approved a settlement between Paramount and California, along with 11 other states that had sued over the planned acquisition. This legal resolution cleared the final major hurdle blocking the deal.
summary: Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison announced the merged company will be called Skydance when it completes its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery next week. A judge approved the settlement Paramount reached with California and 11 other states that sued over the acquisition, clearing the last major hurdle blocking the deal.
author: The Verge

title: Keurig Launches Alta Machine with Plastic‑Free, Compostable Coffee Pucks
content:
Keurig has introduced the Keurig Alta, a new single-serve coffee machine designed to eliminate the use of plastic and aluminum recyclable pods. The company first unveiled the machine and its companion AltaRounds two years ago. These puck-shaped replacements wrap pressed coffee grounds in a plant-based coating derived from seaweed.

The AltaRounds are described as 100 percent compostable. Although they are currently packaged in plastic wrappers to maintain freshness, Keurig is working to transition to paper wrappers, according to CNET.

The Keurig Alta is now available for preorder at a price of $499.99.
summary: Keurig’s new Keurig Alta single‑serve coffee machine uses AltaRounds, puck‑shaped pods made from a seaweed‑derived, plant‑based coating that is 100 percent compostable. The pods currently come in plastic wrappers but the company plans to switch to paper, and the Alta is available for preorder at $499.99.
author: The Verge

title: Tesla adds mid‑charge drive feature after Idaho Supercharger shooting
content:
Tesla has introduced a software update allowing drivers to disengage their vehicles from charging stations in an emergency. This new feature addresses a safety concern that emerged following a mass shooting at a Supercharger location in Twin Falls, Idaho, in August, which resulted in four deaths and seven injuries.

Previously, Tesla vehicles locked the charging plug into the port and disabled the drive function while connected to a charger. To move the car, owners had to manually release the cable from the charging port. Following the Idaho incident, Tesla owners called for a quick-release mechanism to facilitate a faster escape during emergencies.

This week, Tesla responded to those requests by rolling out the software update that enables drivers to drive off mid-charge if necessary.
summary: Tesla released a software update that lets drivers drive off while charging in emergencies. The update was prompted by a mass shooting at a Supercharger in Twin Falls, Idaho that left four dead and seven wounded.
author: The Verge

title: OpenAI launches Dots, a $100/month business-focused assistant
content:
OpenAI has launched Dots, a new agentic assistant that the Verge describes as resembling its competitor, Muse, but tailored for professional use. The service is positioned as a business-first product with a minimum monthly cost of $100. While Dots allows users to create characters similar to those in Muse, its early marketing emphasizes capabilities for completing business tasks, such as launching websites, rescheduling calls, and building slide decks for board meetings.

In contrast, the article notes that Muse focuses more on personal interactions, such as reminding users to purchase items they have viewed. The Vergecast recently discussed Dots and the current state of agentic assistants, highlighting the differing approaches of these two platforms.
summary: OpenAI released Dots this week, a business-first assistant costing a minimum of $100 per month. The product is marketed for tasks such as launching websites, rescheduling calls, and building slide decks for board meetings, contrasting with Muse's personal reminder focus.
author: The Verge

title: Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited PS5 controller features built-in screen and audio mixing
content:
Nacon has announced the Revolution 5 Unlimited, which the company claims is the first officially licensed PlayStation 5 controller featuring a built-in screen. This display allows users to adjust settings, such as joystick sensitivity and button remapping, directly on the gamepad.

The controller’s screen also supports audio mixing from multiple sources. When headphones are connected via a cable, users can simultaneously listen to music from a phone and audio from a PS5 game.

The Revolution 5 Unlimited is currently available for preorder for $229.99 through Nacon’s online store, with shipments expected later this year.
summary: Nacon announced the Revolution 5 Unlimited, which it claims is the first officially licensed PS5 controller with a built-in screen for adjusting settings. The device allows users to mix audio from their phone and console when using wired headphones and is available for preorder at $229.99.
author: The Verge

title: Last Chance: Apply for Side Event at TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026
content:
Less than 24 hours to apply for a Side Event at Founder Summit 2026

The deadline to submit a proposal to host a Side Event at TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 is rapidly approaching. Organizers report that applicants have less than 24 hours left, with the final application window closing tonight at midnight PT.

The Founder Summit will take place in Boston from November 1–7. Hosting a Side Event offers participants the chance to engage directly with the local startup ecosystem, bring their community together, and launch conversations that could shape the future of the region.
summary: Applications for hosting a Side Event at TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 close tonight at midnight PT. The Summit runs from November 1–7 in Boston, inviting participants to connect with the local startup ecosystem.
author: TechCrunch

title: Last 24 Hours to Book Exhibit Table at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
content:
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Final Day to Secure Exhibit Space

Today marks the last day to book an exhibit table for TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. The event will run from October 13–15 at San Francisco’s Moscone West, drawing more than 10,000 founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders. Participants will be on the lookout for companies, products, ideas, and people worth knowing.  

The question for exhibitors remains: will they find your startup?
summary: Today is the last day to book your exhibit table at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. From October 13–15, 10,000+ founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders will arrive at San Francisco’s Moscone West looking for companies, products, ideas, and people worth knowing.
author: TechCrunch

title: Clay CEO Kareem Amin discusses rise of GTM engineer at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
content:
Clay Co‑founder and CEO Kareem Amin will speak at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. He will join the AI Stage to discuss the rise of the GTM engineer.

Attendees can register for a ticket and receive a second pass at 50 % off.
summary: Clay Co-founder and CEO Kareem Amin will speak on the rise of the GTM engineer at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. Attendees can register for a ticket and receive a second pass at 50% off.
author: TechCrunch

title: Jas Khaira of Blackstone to Speak on Next‑Gen AI at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Builders Stage
content:
Blackstone executive Jas Khaira is scheduled to speak on the Builders Stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, where he will discuss building next‑generation artificial intelligence.

The event offers a promotion: attendees can register for a pass and receive 50 % off a second pass.
summary: Jas Khaira of Blackstone will take the Builders Stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 to discuss building next‑gen AI. Registrants can receive a 50% discount on a second pass.
author: TechCrunch

title: Laytr launches app that saves any online content, not just articles
content:
Laytr has launched a new app that expands the range of online content users can store for later use. Unlike tools that focus solely on articles, the app allows users to save articles, recipes, screenshots, videos, PDFs and other items.

The service keeps saved material private and synchronizes the archive across Apple devices, ensuring access wherever users go.
summary: Laytr's new app lets users save articles, recipes, screenshots, videos, PDFs and more for later. The archive remains private and syncs across Apple devices.
author: TechCrunch

title: Pope Leo XIV Criticizes AI-Generated Art
content:
Pope Leo XIV has publicly criticized AI-generated art, stating that it differs fundamentally from human-created works. In a recent statement, he wrote that there is an ontological difference, even before an aesthetic one, between art and what a machine can generate through statistical calculation based on millions of images created by others.

The pope added that algorithms lack the spark of humanity, underscoring his view that machine-produced images cannot replicate the essence of human artistic creation.
summary: Pope Leo XIV says there is an ontological difference between art and what a machine can generate through statistical calculation based on millions of images created by others. He argues that algorithms lack the spark of humanity.
author: TechCrunch

title: Australia Orders Legacy Tech Review After OpenAI Medicare Breach
content:
The Australian government is confronting significant “tech debt” after the OpenAI Medicare breach, a cyber‑attack that exposed vulnerabilities in legacy systems and could lead to a large bill for taxpayers.  

In response, the Home Affairs Department has ordered all federal agencies to conduct a “legacy technology stocktake.” Each agency must develop a plan to reduce legacy technology systems to a level that fits within its risk tolerance and appetite.  

The review is part of a broader effort to fortify defenses against future AI‑agent attacks, and the order was issued this week.
summary: The Australian government has ordered a review of legacy technology after the OpenAI Medicare breach. Agencies must plan to reduce legacy systems to meet risk tolerance, potentially costing taxpayers a large bill.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Brown bear slams into car in Hokkaido, police release dashcam footage
content:
A video released by police shows a brown bear slamming its body against a car in northern Japan. The incident occurred after two bears were spotted on a road in Hokkaido.

The larger bear, believed to be the mother, approached the vehicle before running away with its cub. The driver was unharmed, and police have made dash‑cam footage of the encounter publicly available.
summary: A brown bear slammed its body against a car in northern Japan after two bears were spotted on a road in Hokkaido. The driver was unharmed, the larger bear (believed to be the mother) ran away with its cub, and police released dashcam footage of the encounter.
author: Euronews

title: US sends third carrier strike group to Middle East in biggest buildup since 2003
content:
The United States has dispatched a third carrier strike group to the Middle East, marking the largest buildup in the region since 2003. The move underscores a significant increase in U.S. military presence in the area.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt departed San Diego on Sunday, accompanied by a Marine expeditionary unit of more than 2,000 troops. This deployment brings the potential total U.S. military presence in the region to over 60,000 personnel.
summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt left San Diego on Sunday. It was accompanied by a Marine expeditionary unit of more than 2,000 troops, bringing the potential total US military presence in the region to more than 60,000.
author: Euronews

title: Mobile lab in Butembo, DRC provides Ebola test results within 24 hours
content: A mobile laboratory in Butembo, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, is shortening the time it takes to diagnose Ebola. The facility now delivers test results within 24 hours of sample collection and, on occasion, as quickly as six hours. This rapid turnaround improves patient care and helps contain the spread of the disease.
summary: A mobile laboratory in Butembo, eastern DRC, is accelerating Ebola testing. Results are now available within 24 hours and sometimes as quickly as six.
author: Euronews

title: 5,000 drones create shapes over Nanchang for China's National Day
content:
A fleet of 5,000 drones illuminated the night sky over Nanchang, creating a giant light show as China marked National Day.  

The coordinated display formed shapes that included fighter jets, robots, planes and horses, producing a spectacular visual performance.  

The event was part of the National Day celebrations in the city.
summary: A fleet of 5,000 drones formed fighter jets, robots, planes and horses over Nanchang. The display was part of China's National Day night show.
author: Euronews

title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak kills more than 4,000, officials report
content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak, described as the worst ever in the country, has killed more than 4,000 people, according to official figures released on Friday. The death toll comes from a total of more than 8,000 confirmed cases.

Congolese officials reported the numbers on Friday, highlighting the severe impact of the epidemic across the nation.
summary: The worst ever Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 4,000 people. Congolese officials said on Friday that the outbreak has produced over 8,000 confirmed cases.
author: Euronews

title: U2 mark 50-year anniversary with low‑key surprise gigs in Dublin
content:
U2 marked their 50‑year milestone with a series of surprise, low‑key concerts in Dublin, the band’s hometown.  

Although the group could have filled stadiums for the golden anniversary, they opted to return to their roots and celebrate with intimate gigs in the city where they began.  

The surprise shows underscore the band’s decision to honor half a century of music on a modest, local scale.
summary: U2 are celebrating 50 years as a band. They opted for a few low‑key surprise concerts in their hometown of Dublin instead of large stadium shows.
author: France 24

title: Cornell 7 allegations ignite fury over gang rape culture at Ivy League university
content:
Allegations of a gang rape at an American Ivy League university have ignited a firestorm on social media, prompting widespread criticism of how colleges and universities manage sexual assault cases. The controversy, highlighted under the banner “The Cornell 7,” has drawn intense public scrutiny of campus policies and response mechanisms.

In France, the parliament is debating a major new bill intended to combat violence against women and children. Annette Young interviewed Dr Andreea Gruev‑Vintila, a social psychologist who helped draft the legislation, to discuss its scope and potential impact.

Separately, the king of Morocco announced the appointment of Marrakesh mayor Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the country’s first female prime minister.
summary: Allegations of a gang rape at an American Ivy League university have set social media alight, sparking widespread fury over how colleges handle sexual assault cases. The French parliament is debating a new bill to combat violence against women and children, and Morocco’s king has named Marrakesh mayor Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the country’s first female prime minister.
author: France 24

title: Thousands of Indian women protest after suspected gang rape of 17-year-old in New Delhi
content:
Thousands of women across India have taken to the streets demanding stronger protection for female students after a suspected gang rape of a 17‑year‑old girl in an upscale neighbourhood of New Delhi. The protests, described as a mass movement, call for safer public spaces rather than restrictions on women’s access to them.

In response to the incident, authorities in New Delhi increased protective measures, though demonstrators argue that limiting women’s presence in public areas does not address the root of the problem. The protests underscore a broader demand for improved safety and gender‑based violence prevention nationwide.
summary: Thousands of women have taken to the streets across India demanding better protection for female students after a suspected gang rape of a 17‑year‑old girl in an upscale neighbourhood of New Delhi. Authorities have beefed up protective measures, but the protesters say limiting women's access to public spaces is not the answer.
author: France 24

title: 45-year-old Senator Flavio Bolsonaro ties with President Lula in Brazil election polls
content:
Flavio Bolsonaro, a 45‑year‑old Brazilian senator, has emerged as a presidential candidate who was still relatively unknown in Brazil just a few months ago.  

Recent polling shows Bolsonaro neck and neck with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva as the country heads toward the upcoming presidential election.  

Analysts note that a Bolsonaro victory would place Brazil among a growing list of Latin American nations that have shifted to the right or far right in recent months.
summary: He was still relatively unknown in Brazil a few months ago. The 45-year-old senator is now neck and neck with incumbent President Lula in the polls for the upcoming presidential election.
author: France 24

title: EU states urged to plan gas and electricity savings as fuel prices surge
content:
EU member states have been urged to prepare gas and electricity savings as a harsh winter approaches, amid sharply rising fuel prices across the bloc.  The average price of diesel has climbed to well above €2 per litre, up from roughly €1.50 in October of last year, prompting alarm over the cost‑of‑living impact on households.

The surge in energy costs comes as the conflict in the Middle East adds further pressure, leaving Europeans with limited relief before winter.  EU governments have introduced measures aimed at cushioning ordinary people from the rising prices, and a review is underway to assess the effectiveness of those actions.
summary: EU member states are being urged to prepare gas and electricity savings as diesel prices rise above €2 per litre, up from about €1.50 in October. The article reviews measures to cushion ordinary people from higher energy costs amid a harsh winter and ongoing Middle East conflict.
author: France 24

title: Brazilian voters line up Sunday as merch sales surge for Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro
content:
Nearly 159 million Brazilians are set to vote in general elections on Sunday, choosing new members of parliament, reshaping two‑thirds of the Senate and selecting the country’s next president.  

While the ballot remains secret, supporters are displaying allegiance openly, with flags for candidates and parties lining the streets of Rio de Janeiro. Vendors report a surge in sales of merchandise for incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and his rival Flavio Bolsonaro.  

The report on the merchandising frenzy was filed by France 24’s Brazil correspondent Jan Onoszko.
summary: Nearly 159 million Brazilians will vote in general elections on Sunday, choosing MPs, Senate seats and the president. Vendors in Rio de Janeiro report booming sales of merchandise for President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and rival Flavio Bolsonaro as supporters display flags and apparel.
author: France 24

title: EU Parliament foreign affairs chair McAllister calls for urgent defence gap closure
content:
EU Parliament Foreign Affairs Committee chair David McAllister warned that the European Union must urgently close defence gaps to address growing security threats. In a recent interview, McAllister said the bloc “is not at war with the Russian Federation, but we are no longer at peace with Russia,” underscoring heightened tensions with Moscow.

He added that the EU is still unable to make sovereign decisions in certain defence areas because it remains “too dependent on US capabilities.” The committee chief called for swift action to reduce this reliance and strengthen Europe’s own security posture.
summary: David McAllister, chair of the European Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, said the EU must urgently close defence gaps. He said the EU is not at war with the Russian Federation but is no longer at peace with Russia, and that dependence on US capabilities prevents the EU from making sovereign defence decisions.
author: France 24

title: Lula, 80, runs for fourth term, neck‑and‑neck with Flavio Bolsonaro
content:
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva will stand for re‑election in Brazil on Sunday, seeking a fourth term in office. The 80‑year‑old former steelworker is positioning his campaign around his personal popularity and the country’s recent economic successes.

Lula’s bid places him in a close contest with far‑right rival Flavio Bolsonaro, with both candidates neck‑and‑neck in the latest polls. The race is shaping up as a direct showdown between the incumbent president and Bolsonaro’s challenger.
summary: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, an 80‑year‑old former steelworker, will stand for re‑election on Sunday, seeking a fourth term. He is neck‑and‑neck in the polls with far‑right rival Flavio Bolsonaro.
author: France 24

title: Turkey stock market scandal hits half a million investors
content:
A stock‑market scandal in Turkey is reported to have affected about half a million investors. Authorities say asset managers artificially inflated the value of their funds, prompting investigations.

Turkish officials have carried out multiple arrests linked to the scheme, and a leading lawmaker from the ruling AKP party has resigned in its wake.
summary: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds, sparking a scandal that has affected half a million investors. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.
author: DW World

title: Expedition to Kiribati's Nikumaroro island targets lagoon anomaly in Earhart case
content:
Nearly 90 years after US aviator Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific, a new expedition has been launched to the remote Kiribati island of Nikumaroro.  

The team hopes that an anomaly observed in a lagoon on the island could finally reveal the fate of Earhart’s missing aircraft.  

The expedition marks the latest effort to solve the long‑standing mystery surrounding Earhart’s disappearance.
summary: Nearly 90 years after US aviator Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific, a new expedition has been launched to the remote island of Nikumaroro. The team hopes a lagoon anomaly on the island could finally reveal the fate of her missing aircraft.
author: DW World

title: Argentina launches cash-for-citizenship scheme with $350k gift or $800k bond
content:
Argentina has launched a cash‑for‑citizenship scheme aimed at investors seeking the fastest, though most expensive, path to Argentine citizenship.  

Under the new program, applicants may either make a non‑refundable gift of $350,000 or purchase a government bond for $800,000, depending on their preference and financial strategy.
summary: Argentina has introduced a cash-for-citizenship program that offers the fastest path to Argentine nationality. Investors can obtain citizenship by making a non‑refundable gift of $350,000 or by purchasing a government bond for $800,000.
author: DW World

title: Iran accused of blocking SIM cards and online accounts to silence dissent
content:
DW reports that several Iranians say the government has blocked their SIM cards, bank access and online accounts. According to the interviewees, the restrictions were lifted only after they deleted critical content or pledged to cease activism.

The accounts of the individuals suggest a systematic use of digital controls to silence dissent, with access to essential services contingent on compliance with the demands. No further details were provided.
summary: DW reported that several Iranians said their SIM cards, bank access and online accounts were blocked. The blocks were lifted only after they deleted critical content or pledged to stop activism.
author: DW World

title: Spain's parliament rejects housing bill amid protests over pensioner eviction
content: Spain’s minority government suffered a defeat in parliament after it attempted to push through a pair of emergency measures aimed at making housing more affordable. The measures were introduced in response to a pensioner’s eviction and the protests that followed. The parliamentary vote rejected the bill, halting the government's effort to address the housing affordability crisis.
summary: Spain's minority government was defeated in parliament when its emergency housing measures were rejected. The bid was prompted by a pensioner's eviction and ongoing protests.
author: DW World

title: WHO urges massive aid influx into Gaza ahead of winter amid delayed medicines
content:
The UN World Health Organization (WHO) called on Friday for a massive influx of aid into Gaza before winter, warning that repeated delays in delivering lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and other essential supplies from Israel could have devastating consequences for Palestinians in the war‑torn enclave.

The WHO said the ongoing holdups jeopardize urgent health needs, emphasizing that the lack of timely deliveries threatens the well‑being of residents who depend on these critical resources.
summary: The UN World Health Organization said on Friday that repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and other supplies from Israel into Gaza could have devastating consequences for Palestinians. It appealed for a massive influx of aid before winter.
author: UN News

title: Escalating fighting in Yemen worsens food security crisis, WFP warns
content:
The World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Friday that renewed conflict in Yemen has triggered a surge in hunger, deepening the country’s food security crisis.  

The WFP said the increased hunger could have consequences in the wider region and beyond.  

The agency’s warning underscores the potential regional impact of Yemen’s escalating fighting.
summary: Renewed conflict in Yemen has triggered a surge in hunger. The World Food Programme warned on Friday that the hunger could have consequences in the wider region and beyond.
author: UN News

title: UN rights chief Volker Türk says Haiti gang violence is adapting and expanding
content:
Haitians remain trapped in a cycle of lethal gang violence, according to the United Nations’ top human‑rights official.  

Volker Türk said on Friday that gang violence in Haiti continues to “adapt and expand,” keeping the country in a state of ongoing danger for its residents.
summary: Haitians remain in the grip of lethal gang violence. The UN’s top rights official Volker Türk said on Friday that the violence is adapting and expanding.
author: UN News

title: US Coast Guard intercepts cargo ship Grace carrying fuel to Cuba on Sept. 5
content:
The U.S. Coast Guard announced that it intercepted a large cargo ship carrying fuel bound for Cuba, as the Trump‑era oil embargo on the island remains in effect.  

The vessel, named Grace, was boarded on 5 September in the Caribbean Sea between Cuba and Mexico.  Coast Guard officials said the ship was using tactics to evade authorities and was thought to be part of a common “dark fleet” operation.  The New York Times reported the ship was 91 metres (300 ft) long.  

After boarding, the Grace was taken to Mexico.
summary: The US Coast Guard said it boarded the cargo ship Grace, which was carrying fuel bound for Cuba, and stopped it on 5 September in the Caribbean Sea between Cuba and Mexico. The vessel was using dark fleet tactics to evade authorities and was taken to Mexico as the Trump administration’s oil embargo against Cuba continued.
author: Guardian World

title: India youth ‘cockroach’ protests target Modi’s election chief
content:
India’s youth‑led “cockroach” movement has returned to the streets, directing its protests toward a senior bureaucrat identified as Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s prized election chief.  

The demonstrators are focusing on the official who oversees what is described as the world’s biggest elections, seeking to challenge his role ahead of upcoming polls.
summary: India’s youth protests, referred to as the “cockroach” movement, have returned to the streets. The protests are aimed at Prime Minister Modi’s prized bureaucrat who oversees the world’s biggest elections.
author: Al Jazeera

title: G7 to release 100 million barrels in four months, Trump praises Europe diesel deal
content:
Paris – French President Emmanuel Macron announced that the Group of Seven will release 100 million barrels of oil from strategic reserves over the next four months, with the diesel portion of the release “front‑loaded.”  

In the United States, President Donald Trump praised a separate Europe diesel deal, describing it as a significant achievement.  

The coordinated release is intended to increase diesel supplies while the G7 manages its overall oil reserves.
summary: Macron said the G7 will release 100 million barrels of oil over four months. He added the diesel release will be front‑loaded and Trump hailed the Europe diesel deal.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Spain's parliament rejects housing affordability decrees amid protests
content:
Spain’s parliament rejected two government housing decrees amid mass protests. The measures, presented as a response to a housing‑affordability crisis, were voted down by legislators.

Critics of the proposals argued that the decrees would tighten the housing market rather than alleviate the crisis, leading to their dismissal. The parliamentary decision reflects the opposition to the government’s intended housing reforms.
summary: Spain's parliament rejected both decrees intended to address the housing affordability crisis. Critics said the measures would tighten the housing market.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Cornell University under scrutiny for handling sexual assault allegations
content:
A controversy has erupted around the “Cornell 7,” prompting questions about whether the punishment fits the crime. The dispute centers on the way Cornell University is handling sexual assault allegations.

Critics say the university’s approach to the cases involving the group known as the “Cornell 7” is under scrutiny, raising concerns about the adequacy and fairness of its response.
summary: Cornell’s handling of sexual assault allegations is under scrutiny. The controversy has been described as revolving around the ‘Cornell 7’.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN says three in four households hungry in parts of Yemen amid fighting
content:
The United Nations reports that three in four households are experiencing hunger in parts of Yemen amid ongoing fighting.

The World Food Programme warns that the conflict is displacing thousands of people and cutting off food supplies, creating a “devastating” impact on the population.

These assessments underscore a severe humanitarian crisis in Yemen.
summary: The United Nations says three in four households are hungry in parts of Yemen amid fighting. The World Food Programme warns the conflict is displacing thousands and cutting off food supplies, creating a devastating impact.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Reporter Michael Graczyk says Christa Pike's execution was unlike any he’s seen
content:
Texas reporter Michael Graczyk says he has witnessed nearly 500 executions during his career. He notes that while he has seen botched executions, none have resulted in an inmate surviving the procedure.

Graczyk specifically references the case of Christa Pike, saying it is the first execution he has encountered in which the inmate lived through the process.
summary: Texas reporter Michael Graczyk has witnessed nearly 500 executions, including botched ones. He said Christa Pike's execution was the first in which an inmate survived.
author: BBC World

title: Spanish PM Sánchez loses key housing crisis vote after eviction of 87‑year‑old woman
content:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez suffered a defeat in a key parliamentary vote on the housing crisis after an 87‑year‑old woman was evicted.

The loss has heightened calls for Sánchez to call a snap election, a pressure that follows a series of scandals affecting his party and its allies.
summary: Spanish PM Sánchez lost a key vote on the housing crisis after the eviction of an 87‑year‑old woman. The defeat has increased pressure on him to call a snap election amid scandals affecting his party and allies.
author: BBC World

title: Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko says intensified Russian strikes are tearing Kyiv apart
content:
Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko warned that intensified Russian strikes are tearing the Ukrainian capital apart, describing the situation as “very dramatic” as Russia hits critical infrastructure.  

The mayor’s remarks underscore the severe impact of the attacks on Kyiv’s essential services and the city’s overall stability.
summary: Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko says Kyiv is in a “very dramatic situation.” He says Russia is hitting the city’s critical infrastructure.
author: BBC World

title: New York governor says officials failed Jane Doe, central figure in Cornell rape inquiry
content:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul said the woman at the centre of a Cornell University rape inquiry was “failed” by officials.  

The woman, identified as Jane Doe, alleges she was raped in 2024 by seven students at a fraternity house on the Cornell campus.  

Hochul’s comment came as the university’s investigation into the alleged assault continues.
summary: New York Governor said officials failed Jane Doe, the woman at the centre of a Cornell rape inquiry. Jane Doe alleges she was raped by seven students at a Cornell fraternity house in 2024.
author: BBC World

title: Olivia Dean Faces Lawsuit Over Song Similarities to Bill Withers' Classic
content:
Olivia Dean has been accused of copying Bill Withers’ 1980 hit “Just The Two of Us.”  

Her record label is now facing a lawsuit that claims Dean’s song “I’ve Seen It” contains significant similarities to Withers’ classic.  

The lawsuit alleges that the two tracks are substantially alike, prompting legal action against the label.
summary: Olivia Dean is accused of copying Bill Withers' classic Just The Two of Us. Her record label is sued over similarities between her song I've Seen It and Withers' classic.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Next Generation 2023 lists 60 top world football talents born in 2006
content:
The Next Generation 2023 list highlights 60 of the best young talents in world football, focusing on players born in 2006. The selection includes names such as Warren Zaïre‑Emery and Endrick.

Readers can also check the progress of the series’ other classes, including those from 2022, 2021, 2020, 2019, and 2018.

In addition to the global list, a separate compilation features the 20 best Premier League talents for 2023.
summary: The feature highlights 60 of the best young players worldwide, including Warren Zaïre‑Emery and Endrick. It also points to a separate list of the 20 best Premier League talents.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Slaven Bilic returns as Croatia manager ahead of England test
content:
Slaven Bilic has returned to the spotlight as Croatia’s manager, with a new interview offering a glimpse into his life after leaving the national team. The former West Ham coach was photographed in the lobby of a Canary Wharf hotel, wearing a black Soundgarden T‑shirt and dark denim, and he spoke freely about a range of subjects.

In the interview, Bilic discussed everything from Sir Alex Ferguson’s autobiography and Yugoslav cinema to Nikola Tesla’s celibacy. He also mentioned a recent Metallica concert and steaks at an Argentinian restaurant, sharing off‑record anecdotes that revealed his enjoyment of life in London while preparing for a third Premier League season with West Ham. He noted that he is now “distanced by default, geographically,” indicating his current physical separation from Croatia.

Bilic’s time as Croatia’s manager appears to be a chapter that has closed, though he acknowledges a “bitter‑sweet aftertaste” when reflecting on that period.
summary: Slaven Bilic, the former West Ham United coach, has taken over as Croatia’s manager, replacing Zlatko Dalic. He said the upcoming match against England will be a welcome test for his second spell in charge.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Golden Boy returns to London stage after 40 years with Josh O'Connor
content:
Boxing continues to draw large audiences despite a decline in the sport’s general popularity, largely due to its enduring appeal in storytelling. This connection is highlighted by the London revival of Lillian Hellman’s 1937 play, Golden Boy, which had not been performed in the UK in over 40 years. The drama centers on a young violinist in Depression-era America who abandons his musical talent to pursue fame and wealth in the boxing ring.

The current production features Josh O’Connor in the lead role, a performer known for his film Knives Out and the series Wake Up Dead Man. O’Connor’s portrayal is noted for its physical authenticity, including powerful attacks on a heavy bag that raise concerns for his hands and visible abdominal definition that is not solely the result of makeup. The play’s premise, which blends the disciplines of music and combat, serves as a focal point for examining why boxing remains a box-office success.
summary: The 1937 play Golden Boy, about a violinist who becomes a boxer, is being performed in London for the first time in over 40 years. Josh O'Connor stars in the production, bringing his acting skills to the role of a gifted young man lured into boxing.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester City lodge appeal as FA warns of major implications for game integrity
content: Manchester City has lodged an appeal as the Football Association warned of major implications for the integrity of the game. The development coincides with renewed tensions between the Premier League and the UK prime minister, sparked by an intervention from Andy Burnham in the ongoing debate surrounding Manchester City.
summary: Manchester City has lodged an appeal while the FA warns that the situation has major implications for the integrity of the game. Andy Burnham's intervention in the Manchester City debate has revived tensions between the Premier League and the UK prime minister.

title: Wales win over Norway boosts confidence in Craig Bellamy
content: A 2-1 victory over Norway has sparked discussion about whether the win serves as a turning point for Wales and its head coach, Craig Bellamy. The result appears to have shifted the atmosphere surrounding the team, with observers questioning if the performance has restored fan confidence in Bellamy’s leadership.
summary: Wales secured a 2-1 victory over Norway. The win is viewed as a potential turning point that restored fan confidence in head coach Craig Bellamy.
author: BBC Sport

title: Ferguson Says He Was Terrified by Brain Haemorrhage and Celebrates Return to Manchester United
content:
Former Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson discussed his recovery from a brain haemorrhage during an interview with BBC Breakfast. The conversation took place as he approaches his 85th birthday.

Ferguson described being "terrified" by the medical incident and characterized his return to Manchester United as "fantastic."
summary: Sir Alex Ferguson, former Manchester United manager, says he was terrified by a brain haemorrhage. He also celebrates a fantastic return to Manchester United as he approaches his 85th birthday.

title: Red Bull tipped strongest after Bahrain practice by Russell and Leclerc
content: George Russell and Charles Leclerc have identified Red Bull as the team to beat following the first day of practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix. Both drivers assessed the performance levels during the sessions in Malaysia, pointing to the Austrian team as the current frontrunner.
summary: George Russell and Charles Leclerc say Red Bull is the team to beat after Bahrain practice. The comments came after the first day at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

title: Man City guilty verdict could impact player futures and transfer dealings
content: BBC Sport has examined the potential impact of Manchester City’s guilty verdict on the club’s current squad and its future transfer market activities. The analysis focuses on how this legal outcome may influence the futures of existing players and the team’s broader strategic dealings.
summary: BBC Sport examines the impact of Manchester City's guilty verdict on existing players' futures. It also considers how the verdict will influence the club's transfer market dealings.
author: BBC Sport

title: Over 100 Gen Z candidates run for Congress this cycle, but few win
content:
More than 100 Generation Z candidates launched bids this cycle to run for Congress, according to the Future Caucus. Despite the large number of entrants, few have been successful.

The wave of young candidates underscores a frustration with partisan gridlock and a desire among young adults to enter the political sphere. Their attempts, however, have largely fallen short of securing elected office.
summary: More than 100 Generation Z candidates launched bids for Congress this cycle, per Future Caucus. Few of those candidates have been successful, highlighting young adults' frustration with partisan gridlock.
author: The Hill

title: Trump’s powerful new friends are making MAGA uncomfortable
content: President Trump’s recent appearances with Chinese President Xi Jinping, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D), and Silicon Valley leaders have caused discomfort among his political base. According to GOP strategists, these associations risk alienating MAGA supporters at a critical time as Republicans aim to boost voter turnout ahead of the midterm elections. The article notes that the president has historically enjoyed meeting with powerful figures, even those described as dictators.
summary: Republican strategists state that President Trump's appearances with Chinese President Xi Jinping, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D), and Silicon Valley leaders may turn off his political base. This concern arises as Republicans aim to increase voter turnout ahead of the midterms.
author: The Hill

title: GOP senators warn Trump is hurting Republicans with independents
content:
Senate Republicans have warned that President Trump’s rhetoric is increasingly toxic to independent voters—an electorate deemed critical for winning Senate races in battleground states such as North Carolina, Ohio, Iowa, and Alaska.

Some GOP senators are urging Trump to stay away from key Senate races, cautioning that his presence would likely turn off independent voters and jeopardize Republican prospects. They argue that his involvement could undermine the party’s chances in these competitive contests.

But vulnerable incumbents such as…
summary: Senate Republicans say President Trump has become increasingly toxic with independent voters critical to winning Senate races in battlegrounds. Some GOP senators are warning Trump to stay away from key Senate races, cautioning that his presence would likely turn off independent voters.

title: Cornell Under Scrutiny Over Fraternity Rape Investigation Handling
content:
Cornell University is facing angry calls from politicians, activists and the general public demanding more transparency over how it handled the investigation into a former student’s alleged gang rape.  

The university is under a microscope after a lawsuit was filed in September alleging that a 20‑year‑old student was raped by seven men at a fraternity house.
summary: Cornell University is facing angry calls from politicians, activists, and the public demanding more transparency over its handling of a former student's alleged gang rape. A lawsuit filed in September alleges a 20‑year‑old student was raped by seven men at a fraternity house.
author: The Hill

title: Christa Pike's botched execution in Tennessee sparks death penalty debate
content:
Failed 'torturous' execution attempt on Christa Pike reignites death penalty debate

A botched execution in Tennessee left death‑row inmate Christa Pike alive after she received two doses of lethal injection on Wednesday. The incident has reignited a heated debate about the use of the death penalty in the United States.
summary: Christa Pike survived a botched execution in Tennessee after two doses of lethal injection on Wednesday. The incident has reignited furious debate about the death penalty in the U. S.
author: NPR Politics

title: San Francisco's car crime has plunged. How much credit does Flock deserve?
content:
San Francisco leaders report a dramatic decline in car crime, attributing the drop to AI‑powered cameras that monitor the city’s streets. The city’s officials claim the technology has played a key role in reducing vehicle theft and related offenses.

The article examines the evidence behind the reported success and considers whether the city can continue to rely on its high‑tech surveillance network without compromising civil liberties. It raises questions about the balance between public safety and privacy protections.

The title asks how much credit Flock deserves for the crime reduction, but the article does not provide further details on Flock’s involvement.
summary: San Francisco leaders say AI-powered cameras helped drive a dramatic decline in car crime. We examine the evidence — and whether the city can keep its high-tech dragnet without sacrificing civil liberties.
author: NPR Politics

title: Australia, COP31 co‑host, urged to tax polluters for climate damage
content: Australia, co‑hosting the upcoming COP31 summit, has been urged to require polluters to pay for climate damage. Climate Home News notes that UN climate funds are running short on cash, creating a need for new revenue streams. The article argues that now is the time to start taxing companies whose emissions are driving harm in the Pacific and other vulnerable parts of the world.
summary: The Climate Home News article notes UN climate funds are short on cash and calls for taxing companies whose emissions are harming the Pacific and other vulnerable regions. It argues that, as a co‑host of COP31, Australia should make its polluters pay for climate damage.
author: Climate Home News

title: RNA urine test outperforms standard bladder cancer tests and could help guide treatment
content:
Researchers at Stanford Medicine and the VA Palo Alto Health Care System have developed a urine test that diagnoses bladder cancer more accurately than current standard methods. This new diagnostic tool utilizes RNA analysis to provide superior precision in identifying the disease.

Beyond diagnosis, the test enables physicians to evaluate how a patient’s cancer responds to treatment. It also helps predict whether immunotherapy or chemotherapy is likely to be the most effective therapeutic option for each individual patient.
summary: A simple urine test devised by researchers at Stanford Medicine and the VA Palo Alto Health Care System can diagnose bladder cancer more accurately than current standard methods. The test also allows physicians not only to assess the cancer's response to treatment but also to predict whether immunotherapy or chemotherapy is likely to be most effective for each patient.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Low-calorie diet and exercise put early-onset type 2 diabetes in remission for 54% of participants
content:
New research presented at the Annual Meeting of The European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) in Milan, Italy, indicates that early-onset type 2 diabetes can be reversed in approximately half of affected individuals. The study, which also appeared in The Lancet Regional Health Americas journal, focused on patients under the age of 45 who developed the condition. The findings suggest that a combination of a low-energy diet and a structured exercise program was effective in putting the disease into remission for 54% of the participants.

The EASD conference took place from September 28 to October 2.
summary: New research presented at the EASD Annual Meeting in Milan shows that low-energy diets combined with structured exercise can reverse early-onset type 2 diabetes in about half of participants. The study, appearing in The Lancet Regional Health Americas, focused on individuals under 45 years old who developed the condition.
author: Medical Xpress

title: How AI is redefining Wall Street jobs — and boosting demand for this new 'hottest skill' by 1,721%
content:
Banks are driving a sharp increase in demand for AI engineers, according to recent reports. The focus is on a specific capability known as "agent orchestration," which involves coordinating teams of specialized AI agents to perform complex tasks.

The hiring surge is concentrated in the financial sector, where firms are looking for engineers who can design and manage these orchestrated agent systems. This skill set is becoming essential for modern Wall Street operations.

The demand for this new "hottest skill" has risen by 1,721%, highlighting the rapid expansion of AI roles within banks and the broader financial industry.
summary: Banks are fueling a hiring surge for AI engineers who are good at "agent orchestration" — the ability to coordinate teams of specialized agents.
author: CNBC Business

title: Astronauts reach ISS on record‑speed US express flight
content:
Four astronauts arrived at the International Space Station on Thursday after launching on an eight‑hour express flight that set a U.S. speed record.  

The mission, described as the quickest U.S. express flight to the ISS, saw the crew pull up at the station after the record‑breaking journey.  

The arrival marks the fastest U.S. express flight to the International Space Station to date.
summary: Four astronauts pulled up at the International Space Station on Thursday. Their eight‑hour express launch set a U.S. speed record.
author: Phys.org

title: EU Climate Monitor Reports 52% of Europe Exposed to Record Heat Stress
content:
Europe’s record‑setting summer has left more than half of the continent under intense heat stress, according to the EU’s climate monitor.  

The monitor reported that a record 52 % of Europe was exposed to intense heat stress during the exceptionally hot summer that seared the continent this year, as stated on Friday.
summary: The EU's climate monitor reported that 52% of Europe was exposed to intense heat stress during the exceptionally hot summer. This record level of heat stress was noted in a statement released on Friday.
author: Phys.org

title: Penn State Study Proposes Scalable AI Marketing Content Deployment
content:
Marketers are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence (AI) tools to create content and improve workflow efficiency.  

A new study by a Penn State researcher and collaborators proposes an approach to deploying AI‑generated marketing content at scale while reducing the need for costly and time‑consuming traditional testing.  

The study offers a new method for scaling AI‑generated marketing content.
summary: A new study by a Penn State researcher and collaborators proposes an approach to deploying AI-generated marketing content at scale. The approach aims to reduce the need for costly and time‑consuming traditional testing.
author: Phys.org

title: Quantum computing must differentiate from AI, says columnist Karmela Padavic-Callaghan
content:
Quantum computing experts warn that the technology must carve out a distinct identity from artificial intelligence to achieve large‑scale success, writes columnist Karmela Padavic‑Callaghan.  

Padavic‑Callaghan notes that, despite this need for differentiation, the public often conflates quantum computing with AI, blurring the two fields in popular perception.
summary: Columnist Karmela Padavic-Callaghan says quantum computing must differentiate itself from AI to succeed at scale. The public already sees the two technologies as mixed up.
author: New Scientist

title: Excerpt from Emily St. John Mandel's Exit Party Introduces 2031 Los Angeles
content: Emily St. John Mandel’s new novel Exit Party has been selected as the October read for the New Scientist Book Club. The book’s opening introduces readers to Los Angeles in 2031, where a curfew is being lifted from the city.
summary: The opening of Emily St. John Mandel's new novel Exit Party, selected as the October read for the New Scientist Book Club, sets the scene in Los Angeles in 2031. The story begins as a curfew lifts from the city.
author: New Scientist

title: Brain area discovered that may be critical for viable pregnancies
content: A newly identified region of the brain has been shown to be essential for successful embryo implantation in mice. Researchers found that this part of the brain is required for the implantation process, which is a critical step in establishing a viable pregnancy. The discovery may help explain why some pregnancies and in‑vitro fertilization (IVF) attempts fail.
summary: Researchers found a newly discovered part of the brain essential for successful embryo implantation in mice. This finding may explain why some pregnancies and IVF attempts fail.
author: New Scientist

title: SpaceX eight‑hour express flight led by Jessica Watkins sets US speed record
content:
Four astronauts reached the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday after an eight‑hour express flight that set a U.S. speed record. The mission was led by commander Jessica Watkins, the first Black woman to command a crew to orbit.

SpaceX launched the crew from Cape Canaveral at 11:10 am (1510 GMT) following a three‑week delay to repair a leaking fuel system in the Dragon capsule. Thick clouds had threatened to halt the countdown earlier that morning, but skies cleared in time for a safe liftoff.

content:

content:

The piece examines the motivations of listeners and viewers who are turning to physical formats such as compact discs, DVDs and vinyl records as an alternative to algorithm‑driven streaming services.

The article was linked on Hacker News, where the discussion has earned 9 points and generated 2 comments.

title: New competition rewards participants for lowering their biological age
content:
A new contest pits competitors against each other in a race to biological youth

The author announced that they have officially signed up for an unusual competition that rewards participants for getting younger. The competition focuses on competitors’ biological ages, which are intended to provide a better way to measure age-related changes.

The author recently turned 40 and noted that while time and chronological age only move forward, the contest’s emphasis is on biological age. No further details about the competition’s structure or prizes were provided.
summary: The author, who recently turned 40, signed up for a competition that rewards competitors for reducing their biological age. The contest focuses on biological age metrics as an alternative way to measure youth.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Hospital and radiology network blame Palantir scheduling software for errors and burnout
content:
A hospital giant and a radiology network adopted Palantir’s software to streamline their scheduling processes.  

Nurses and other staff members say the new system has introduced errors, increased burnout, and generated frustration among frontline workers.  

The criticism highlights growing concerns that the technology intended to improve efficiency is instead creating additional challenges for health‑care personnel.
summary: A hospital giant and a radiology network adopted Palantir software to streamline scheduling. Nurses and other staff say the new software is causing errors, burnout and frustration.
author: Wired

title: Patched flaw in ChatGPT Mac app could have let hackers steal sensitive data
content:
A vulnerability in the Mac version of the ChatGPT app was recently patched, highlighting a potential avenue for hackers to obtain sensitive data.  

The flaw, if exploited, could have allowed unauthorized access to user information, underscoring that AI software itself can be an inviting and vulnerable target.  

The incident comes as attention remains focused on the hacking capabilities of AI agents, reminding stakeholders that the applications powering these agents may also contain security weaknesses.
summary: A vulnerability in the ChatGPT Mac app was recently patched. The flaw could have let hackers grab sensitive data, showing AI software is an inviting and vulnerable target.
author: Wired

title: Election deniers label GOP midterm polling a psyop
content:
Election deniers have claimed that the GOP’s poor midterm polling is a “psyop.”  According to reports, dozens of high‑profile MAGA influencers and pundits have weighed in on the issue.  

Catturd posted on X that “The laughable fake polls are rolling out.”
summary: Dozens of high‑profile MAGA influencers and pundits have weighed in on the claim. Catturd posted on X that the polls are “laughable fake polls” rolling out.

title: Waymo, Zoox and Tesla driverless cabs have cameras pointing at riders
content:
Self‑driving cars from Waymo, Zoox, and Tesla are equipped with a network of cameras and sensors.  

The vehicles are studded with these devices, which are used to navigate and monitor the surrounding environment.  

Some of the cameras and sensors are positioned to point directly at riders.
summary: Self‑driving cars from Waymo, Zoox and Tesla are studded with cameras and sensors. Some of those cameras are aimed at the riders.
author: Wired

title: AI music platform Suno launches public beta for speech generation
content:
SunO, the AI music‑generation platform, has added a new feature that produces spoken voices from scripts or prompted descriptions. The speech capability is now available in public beta on SunO’s web and mobile platforms and can generate voiceovers and background music at the same time.

In the announcement, SunO chief product officer Jack Brody said, “Music will always be at the heart of SunO and what we build. At the same time, our vision has always extended to other forms of human expression. Today, we’re expanding what’s possible in SunO with Speech: the first audio model that generates voice and music to …”

The full story was reported by The Verge.
summary: Suno introduced a public‑beta feature that generates spoken voices from scripts or prompts, announced by chief product officer Jack Brody. The speech tool can produce voiceovers together with background music on Suno’s web and mobile platforms.
author: The Verge

title: SpaceX launches Jessica Watkins and crew to ISS after fuel leak delay
content:
SpaceX successfully launched a four‑astronaut crew to the International Space Station on Thursday, marking the start of a mission that is slated to continue until spring. The launch came after a three‑week postponement to repair a leaking fuel system in the crew capsule.

Commander Jessica Watkins, the first Black woman to lead a crew to orbit, made her second trip to the space station. The crew also includes a Canadian astronaut whose wife is expected to give birth while he is away.

Thick morning clouds threatened to halt the countdown, but conditions cleared sufficiently to allow a safe liftoff. The mission proceeds under NASA’s oversight following the resolved technical issues.
summary: SpaceX lifted off commander Jessica Watkins and three other astronauts to the International Space Station on Thursday. The launch, delayed three weeks to fix a leaking fuel system, proceeded after clouds cleared and will keep the crew on the station until spring.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon AI model only to vetted cybersecurity experts
content:
Google has announced the release of its latest artificial‑intelligence model, Gemini 4 Argon, but has limited access to a vetted group of cybersecurity experts. The move is intended to prevent potential misuse of the technology by hackers.

The company said it would withhold Gemini 4 Argon from the public for now, making it available only to the selected experts. This restricted release is part of a phased approach to safely introduce frontier AI capabilities.

In a blogpost announcing the model, Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google’s chief AI architect, wrote, “Safely releasing frontier capabilities at this level requires a phased approach.”
summary: Google said it will withhold its most powerful AI model from the public and release Gemini 4 Argon only to a vetted group of cybersecurity experts. Chief AI architect Koray Kavukcuoglu said the phased approach is needed to prevent misuse by hackers.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Feeld founders receive record £3.8m dividend after 32% sales rise
content:
Feeld, the UK‑based dating platform for non‑monogamous, queer and kinky users, announced a record £3.8 million dividend for its founders after a sharp rise in sales.  

The company said revenue jumped 32 % to £64 million, with users outside the United Kingdom contributing nearly 90 % of that income. Feeld attributes the growth to “open‑minded people exploring love, desire and alternative relationships in a safe, inclusive space,” drawing users away from more mainstream rivals.  

The £3.8 million payout represents the app’s largest dividend to date, reflecting the recent surge in interest and financial performance.
summary: Feeld, a UK‑based dating app for non‑monogamous, queer and kinky users, reported revenues jumped 32% to £64 million. The growth enabled the company to pay a record £3.8 million dividend to its founders.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Lobbyist Martha Dalton helped Andy Burnham become PM via Makerfield byelection
content:
A lobbyist who recently represented the US technology firm Palantir is reported to have played a senior role in the political rise of Andy Burnham. Martha Dalton, whose consultancy Lodestone provided services to Palantir in 2024 and 2025, was involved in Burnham’s campaign during the Makerfield by‑election that returned him to parliament.

Dalton worked closely with Burnham’s team on strategic communications and rebuttals for the by‑election. After the victory, she was among the supporters who clapped Burnham into Downing Street in July.

The involvement of Dalton, a recent Palantir lobbyist, is cited as a key factor in Burnham’s successful bid to become prime minister.
summary: Martha Dalton, whose firm Lodestone worked for Palantir in 2024 and 2025, campaigned for Andy Burnham in the Makerfield byelection that secured his return to parliament. She coordinated strategic communications and rebuttals with Burnham’s team and was among supporters who clapped him into Downing Street in July.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Christa Pike in critical condition after Tennessee botched execution
content:
Christa Pike is in critical condition following a botched execution in Tennessee, her lawyer said.  

Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed 19‑year‑old Colleen Slemmer at a job‑training camp for young people.  

The lawyer confirmed Pike’s condition remains critical after the execution attempt.
summary: Pike is in critical condition following a botched execution in Tennessee, according to her lawyer. She was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed 19‑year‑old Colleen Slemmer at a job training camp for young people.
author: Euronews

title: FlyDubai captain Smit Machchhar recounts cockpit attack and fight to regain control
content:
A FlyDubai captain who helped avert a disaster is speaking publicly about the incident while recovering in hospital. Capt. Smit Machchhar described the moment he fought to regain control of the cockpit after the aircraft entered a steep descent.

The pilot said he was “fighting for his life” but knew he had to get back up to prevent a tragedy on the FlyDubai flight.
summary: Capt. Smit Machchhar is still recovering in hospital after helping prevent a tragedy on a FlyDubai flight. He said he was “fighting for his life” as he worked to regain control of the cockpit during a steep descent.
author: Euronews

title: Uzbekistan wins gold at record-breaking Chess Olympiad in Samarkand
content:
Uzbekistan captured the gold medal at the record‑breaking Chess Olympiad held in Samarkand, winning on home soil.

The tournament featured almost 400 teams representing more than 190 countries and was contested over 11 rounds.

Germany secured the bronze medal, while Hungary, France, Spain, Azerbaijan and Armenia also finished among the top ten teams.
summary: Uzbekistan captured the gold medal at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand. The competition featured almost 400 teams from more than 190 countries over 11 rounds, with Germany taking bronze and Hungary, France, Spain, Azerbaijan and Armenia finishing in the top ten.
author: Euronews

title: World's tallest wind turbine, 365 m, installed in Schipkau, Germany
content:
Germany has installed a new wind turbine that, at 365 metres tall, is the world’s tallest.

The turbine stands in Schipkau and was designed to capture stronger winds at its record height.

It is scheduled to begin operating in November.
summary: Germany’s new 365‑metre wind turbine in Schipkau is the world’s tallest. It is designed to capture stronger winds and will start operating in November.
author: Euronews

title: Houthis reject Saudi claim drone hit electricity station powering Prophet's Mosque
content:
Saudi-led coalition officials said a drone struck the Taibah electricity distribution station, which provides power to the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, one of Islam’s holiest sites.  

The coalition linked the attack to the Houthi movement, alleging the group targeted the holy site’s infrastructure.  

The Houthis rejected the allegation, calling it a “lie” intended to support previous accusations against them.
summary: The Saudi-led coalition said a drone struck the Taibah electricity distribution station that supplies power to the Prophet's Mosque in Medina. The Houthis called the allegation a "lie" and denied targeting the holy site.
author: Euronews

title: Pete Hegseth establishes Pentagon Office of Religious Affairs reporting to him
content:
Pete Hegseth has established a Pentagon Office of Religious Affairs that reports directly to him.  

Since taking the role, Hegseth has infused his evangelical Christianity into his leadership of the department, hosting worship services for employees and frequently describing the United States as a Christian nation.
summary: Pete Hegseth created a Pentagon Office of Religious Affairs that reports directly to him. He has infused his evangelical Christianity into his Pentagon leadership, hosting worship services for employees and often describing the United States as a Christian nation.
author: Euronews

title: Thousands attend secret New York Dîner en Blanc with Parisian Belle Époque theme
content:
Thousands of participants dressed in white gathered at a secret location in New York for Dîner en Blanc, the city’s annual outdoor dinner.  

The event, which celebrates a Parisian Belle Époque theme, transformed the hidden venue into a large, white‑clad gathering for the annual celebration.
summary: Thousands of participants dressed in white gathered at a secret New York location for Dîner en Blanc. The dinner is an annual outdoor event with a Parisian Belle Époque theme.
author: Euronews

title: France and Spain aim to reinforce bilateral ties as Europe's power shifts east
content:
France and Spain are working to strengthen their bilateral ties as Europe’s balance of power shifts eastward. The effort is highlighted by French President Emmanuel Macron’s recent visit to Spain, which political scientist Carlos Mascarell Vilar, based in Spain, says must be viewed through the lenses of European power, political legacy and geoeconomics.

According to Delano D’Souza, who welcomed Mascarell Vilar, the Madrid‑Paris axis is being reinforced at a time when eastern European nations such as Poland are gaining influence. Macron’s push to deepen the Franco‑Spanish partnership is presented as part of a broader strategy to advance European defence and strategic sovereignty.
summary: France and Spain are seeking to reinforce their bilateral relationship as Europe’s balance of power moves toward eastern countries such as Poland. Macron’s visit to Spain is intended to strengthen the Madrid‑Paris axis as part of a broader effort to advance European defence and strategic sovereignty.
author: France 24

title: Éric Fassin frames French student protests as demand for dignity and equal study conditions
content:
Parisian student protests have grown into a broader movement demanding “respect, dignity and decent working conditions,” according to sociologist Éric Fassin.  

Alison Sargent welcomed Fassin, a professor at Paris VIII University, who described the demonstrations as a call for equality, dignity and recognition. He noted that students from working‑class suburbs are pressing for the basic conditions that enable study and for the same opportunities enjoyed by students elsewhere.  

Fassin said the unrest, which began among students in the Parisian suburbs and has since spread, constitutes a social movement with a political and democratic dimension. He also placed the protests within a longer history of repression of social movements in France.
summary: Éric Fassin, a sociologist and professor at Paris VIII University, said the French student protests are a demand for equality, dignity and recognition. He noted that students from working‑class suburbs are seeking basic conditions that make studying possible and the same opportunities as other students, viewing the movement as a social and democratic response within a history of repression.
author: France 24

title: Bamo Nouri says US withdrawal from Iraq will boost Iran's influence
content:
America is withdrawing its military forces from Iraq, a move that experts say could shift the country’s balance of power in favor of Iran. The departure is seen as a strategic and tactical mistake that may leave Iraq more vulnerable to Iranian influence.

Erin Ogunkeye, who welcomed investigative journalist Bamo Nouri—an Honorary Research Fellow in the Department of International Politics at City Saint George's University of London—argues that the end of the American presence is a profound shift. He notes that the key issue is not whether Iraq has formally regained sovereignty, but whether it has the political cohesion, security capacity and economic independence to exercise that sovereignty. Ogunkeye points out that Tehran’s influence is already embedded within Iraq’s political parties, armed groups, economic networks and financial system, meaning its power does not depend on a conventional military presence. Removing the American counterweight could give Iran‑backed groups more room to operate, while leaving Iraq’s Kurdish region—reliant on American military, intelligence and air‑defence support—facing strategic uncertainty.

The withdrawal may intensify Iran’s role in Iraq and make the country’s attempts at political and economic reform considerably more difficult.
summary: Bamo Nouri, investigative journalist and Honorary Research Fellow at City Saint George's University of London, says the end of the American military presence in Iraq marks a profound shift in the country's balance of power. He warns that Iran’s embedded influence could expand as the US leaves, creating strategic uncertainty for the Kurdish region and hindering Iraq’s political and economic reforms.
author: France 24

title: Brazil's gun lobby backs Bolsonaro as elections approach
content:
Brazil is heading to the polls amid a debate over firearms access that could sway voters in the rural south. The issue has gained prominence as the country prepares for the upcoming elections.

Under President Jair Bolsonaro, Brazil became more heavily armed than ever before. The number of registered hunters, shooters and collectors—known by the acronym “CACs”—rose sevenfold in four years, according to the report.  

Opposition leader Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has pledged to reverse this trend, a move that has irritated the powerful gun lobby. France 24’s team in Brazil reported on the developments.
summary: Brazil is heading to elections, and the issue of firearms could influence votes, especially in the rural south. Under Bolsonaro, the number of registered hunters, shooters and collectors (CACs) increased sevenfold in four years, a trend Lula promised to reverse, irritating the powerful gun lobby.

title: Eritrea Cuts Diplomatic Ties with Ethiopia Over Embassy Closure
content:
Eritrea has severed all diplomatic relations with Ethiopia after Addis Ababa ordered the closure of its embassy in Asmara and declared ten Eritrean diplomats persona non grata on Thursday.  

The Ethiopian decision to expel the diplomats and shut its mission prompted the Eritrean government in Asmara to cut ties, citing the move as a breach of diplomatic protocol.  

The diplomatic fallout followed overnight blasts heard in Addis Ababa, which raised concerns that renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia could spread.
summary: Ethiopia ordered the closure of its embassy in Eritrea and declared 10 Eritrean diplomats persona non grata. In response, Asmara severed all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia after overnight blasts in Addis Ababa raised fears of renewed conflict.

content:

title: EU fully rejects US threat to ban diesel exports unless fuel stocks released
content:
The European Union on Friday “fully” rejected a United States threat to ban diesel exports unless the bloc releases additional fuel stocks, an EU official said.

The official’s statement emphasized that the EU pushes back against the proposed ban and will not comply with the demand to increase fuel stock releases.
summary: The European Union on Friday pushed back against a US threat to ban any diesel exports unless the bloc releases more of its fuel stocks. An EU official said the EU “fully” rejected the move.

title: Refugee education funding cuts threaten millions, teenage Sudanese girl seeks tech degree
content:
I have not lost my dreams: Refugee education funding cuts threaten millions

A teenage girl who fled war‑torn Sudan for neighbouring Egypt and hopes to pursue a technology degree is an example of why countries must ensure that young refugees can continue to learn. The story illustrates the broader impact of cuts to refugee education funding, which threaten the educational prospects of millions of displaced youth.
